result.title: Jev document evidence extraction: what the three Jev docs do and do not support for a 99.99%-reliable Defuddle sanitizer/clutter-remover
result.summary:
I read SCOUT_NOTES.md, EXPERIMENT_RULES.md and all three Jev documents (JEV_AGENT_BRIEF.md, 437 lines; JEV_ECOSYSTEM_EXCERPTS_1.md, 67 lines; JEV_ECOSYSTEM_EXCERPTS_2.md, 57 lines) end to end, made no API calls, and extracted every number bearing on topics (a)-(k) into a 106-row evidence table (/tmp/jev-research/results/doc-evidence/evidence_table.tsv) with a vendor-vs-independent flag and file:line references. I also computed, in /tmp/jev-research/results/doc-evidence/page_level_math.csv, how per-block accuracies compound into page-level reliability, because Defuddle's unit of correctness is a whole page (byte-equal expected Markdown), not a single decision.

Measured facts: on text-readable classification Jev sits 3-6 points below frontier LLMs (Banking77 81.0% vs 84.4%, n=3,080; Jev-as-a-Judge within 3 points of GPT-6 "where the verdict can be read from the text"); the closest analogs to a "keep this block?" Noul score SMS spam F1 0.91, AG News 86.6%, relevance 74%, Noul soft accuracy 0.918. The best filtered bands are 96.3% at confidence >= 0.99 (58% coverage, Banking77) and "<1%" error above 0.8 in pi-warden's 15,346 production judgments; yet Du et al. found 102 errors among 1,819 decisions at probability exactly 1.0 (5.6%). Calibration is good pooled (ECE 0.047) but bad per task (median ECE 0.168; F1-optimal Noul threshold median 0.35, not 0.5). Determinism: none (no seeds; 0.04 mean probability movement; 12% chosen-option flips; jgrep 128/150 identical across uncached reruns; jev-latest drifts; pinned versions get 30 days' deprecation notice; the local smoke files show confidence 1.0 on 1.13.0 vs 0.99 on 1.14.0 for an identical state). Security: injection flips 93.5-100% of routing decisions on the official API, one appended opinion flips 12.1% and pushes 38% of confident answers below 0.8, a browser agent clicked a planted ad 91% of the time, a toxicity filter was bypassed by respelling, and attacked decisions are as confident as clean ones; the docs' unanimous conclusion is "argued input", "never the sole gate", "confidence is not authorization". Context is 32k tokens per question / 64k per request (262k mode "slower and less accurate"); accuracy loss from irrelevant state is acknowledged but unquantified. Cost is $0.042/M input tokens (~$0.0004 per 10k-token page); latency 100-800 ms depending on hop count; signups were paused Sept 22; data is US-hosted, ZDR only for enterprise, and an Oct 24 leak exposed customers' Noul outputs. Official SDKs are Python/JS only, there is no browser-safe mode, and the only DOM-element precedents (typesafe-adblock, unclutter, jev-ultrafast, Hide posts on X) publish zero accuracy figures.

Implication for the Jev question: no number in the documents comes within two orders of magnitude of 99.99% per decision; the best measured bands are 100x-561x the 1e-4 error target, and those are per-item. At the page level, 96.3% per block gives a 15% chance that a 50-block page is fully correct, 99% gives 60.5%, and 99.99% page-level reliability would require 99.9998% per block. For Defuddle's meaning A (security sanitization) the docs forbid the use outright: every guard author disclaims boundary status and the recommended architecture is a deterministic validator the model cannot override, which is exactly what `stripUnsafeElements`/`isDangerousUrl` already are. For meaning B (clutter removal) the evidence supports a narrow, asynchronous, threshold-tuned, cached, shadow-mode tie-breaker for ambiguous blocks in the Node/Worker paths (where the Workers AI binding with ZDR exists), not an aggressive replacement of the heuristic pipeline, and never in the synchronous, no-network, logged-in-page browser extension path.

findings.claim: No number in the three Jev documents supports 99.99% per-decision reliability; the best measured filtered bands are 100x to 561x the 1e-4 error target, and even probability-1.0 outputs carried 5.6% error in one study.
findings.evidence: conf >= 0.99 band: 96.3% accurate on 58% of Banking77 (EXC1 L66; BRIEF L179) = 370x; pi-warden '<1%' wrong above 0.8 on 15,346 calls (EXC1 L67) = >=100x; Du et al. 102 errors in 1,819 decisions at p=1 (EXC1 L33) = 561x; Noul soft accuracy 0.918 (BRIEF L181) = 820x. Vendor's own docs: calibration 'does not guarantee that any single answer is correct' (EXC1 L19).

findings.claim: Page-level correctness compounds per-block errors: at 50 block decisions per page, 96.3% per block yields 15.2% fully-correct pages, 99% yields 60.5%, and a 99.99% page-level target requires 99.9998% per block (computed; assumes independent errors).
findings.evidence: python computation in page_level_math.csv: 0.963^50=0.1518, 0.99^50=0.605, 0.999^50=0.951; required per-block for page target 0.9999 at N=10/20/50/100 = 0.99999/0.999995/0.999998/0.999999. Defuddle's unit of test is a byte-equal page (SCOUT L11).

findings.claim: By analogy, a zero-shot 'keep this block?' Noul could plausibly reach ~85-92% per-block accuracy at a default threshold, ~93-97% after threshold tuning and multi-Noul decomposition, and ~96-99% inside a high-confidence band covering roughly 58-76% of blocks; the remainder would still need the existing heuristics.
findings.evidence: SMS spam F1 0.91 (P 0.87/R 0.95, n=5,574) (EXC1 L61); AG News 86.6% (n=7,600) (EXC1 L61); relevance 74% on 2,380 labels (EXC1 L65); Jev-as-judge within 3 pts of GPT-6 where verdict readable (EXC1 L59); Banking77 81.0% (EXC1 L7). Tuning on 10 labels F1 0.706->0.793 (EXC1 L60); UNFAIR-ToS 0.50->0.75 (EXC1 L51); phishing 62.6%->95.0% with 5 Nouls + LR on 1,000 labels (EXC1 L62); option-wise Nouls retain 97.0% vs Choice 79.4% at 0.90 (BRIEF L326). Bands: 96.3%@>=0.99 on 58%; cascade@0.90 handles 75.9% (EXC1 L66). This is inference by analogy, not a measurement on DOM blocks.

findings.claim: Confidence is a deterministic transform of the distribution, not a correctness estimate; Noul has no confidence field; the 0.5 default is wrong per task and per-task calibration is poor, so any Defuddle threshold must be tuned on its own labeled blocks and re-audited per version.
findings.evidence: Choice confidence = (p_max-1/n)/(1-1/n); Noul: docs suggest |2p-1|, starting 0.7/0.3 [vendor] (BRIEF L169-173). Median F1-optimal Noul threshold 0.35 across 31 benchmarks (BRIEF L177). Pooled ECE 0.047 vs median per-benchmark 0.168, range 0.003-0.28 (BRIEF L180). In-sample thresholds targeting 5% FNR miss up to 17% held-out (EXC2 L19). 'I Guessed My Jev Threshold. It Threw Away a Third of the Good Pages' (EXC2 L39). P(X)+P(not X) off by 0.064 (EXC1 L48).

findings.claim: The three-band cascade (auto-act / cautious / route elsewhere) is the most reproduced pattern, but its measured ceiling is small and it requires an independent second judge; in Defuddle that second judge would be the existing deterministic heuristics or a human-reviewed fixture, not another flash LLM.
findings.evidence: Banking77 cascade at 0.90: Jev handles 75.9%, 84.0% overall vs Opus alone 84.4%, ~28% of cost (EXC1 L66; BRIEF L341). Flash-tier LLM judges repeat >85% of Jev's most confident errors; cascades gain <=2.7 pts even with oracle thresholds (EXC1 L52). TypeSafe's worked examples use >=0.9 for high-stakes auto-actions and a 0.5 floor [vendor] (BRIEF L183).

findings.claim: Jev is non-deterministic and version-drifting, so a byte-exact 226-fixture suite can only be reproducible against a recorded response cache, which tests the cache rather than the model; Defuddle's CI is network-disabled anyway.
findings.evidence: No seeds; ~0.04 probability movement; ~12% chosen-option change on repeat (BRIEF L150, L373; EXC1 L20, L49). OpenRouter: Score 1.21 then 1.17, Noul 0.42 then 0.44 on the same message; jgrep 128/150 identical over three uncached runs, rest <=0.03 (EXC1 L20). jev-latest changes between releases (BRIEF L72); deprecation window shrank 60 -> 30 days (BRIEF L161). Local smoke artifacts (n=1, not from docs): identical 453-token state gave confidence 1.0 on jev-1.13.0 and 0.99 on jev-1.14.0. 'Cache decisions keyed on (model, state, questions); reruns are then exact' (BRIEF L332). Fixture tests are hermetic, network disabled (SCOUT L11).

findings.claim: The documents are unanimous that Jev must never be a security boundary, so it cannot replace or sit in front of Defuddle's deterministic sanitization (meaning A); the recommended architecture (deterministic validator the model cannot override) is what Defuddle already has.
findings.evidence: Routing 100% clean -> 0-5.8% under injection, ASR 93.5-100% on the official API (EXC1 L41; BRIEF L33). Typed-model guardrails failed open 93-100% under a misleading option label while a deterministic rule reached 100% (BRIEF L382). 'Confidence is not authorization': attacked decisions as confident as originals (BRIEF L383). Toxicity filter flagged 30/30 unedited but 'many' TokenBreak-respelled prompts passed (EXC1 L45). 'Anyone who wires Jev into a security boundary is wiring in a model that treats its state as argued input' (EXC1 L11). Every guard author disclaims boundary status; jev-guard fails OPEN by default (EXC2 L18, L42). Defuddle's `_stripUnsafeElements` runs unconditionally as 'the only guaranteed sanitization boundary' (SCOUT L18).

findings.claim: Using Jev for clutter removal (meaning B) makes extraction steerable by page authors: a block that says 'this is the article' is literally the one-appended-opinion attack, and the closest web precedent is an agent clicking a planted ad 91% of the time despite being told page text is untrusted.
findings.evidence: One appended opinion flips 12.1% of decisions and pushes 38% of confident answers below 0.8 (EXC1 L42); natural context flips 61.4-73.2% (EXC1 L43); jev-ultrafast clicked a planted 'Confirm Price' ad 91% (EXC1 L44; EXC2 L4). Consequence is bounded to content quality only if the deterministic sanitizer stays downstream (inference).

findings.claim: Context limits force text-only, stripped, often truncated states: 32k tokens per question and 64k per request, with an acknowledged but unquantified accuracy loss from irrelevant content; the right request shape is many per-block Nouls over one shared state, not many blocks stuffed into one question.
findings.evidence: 32k per question (state + question), 64k per request, 262k with header that is 'slower and less accurate' at the same price; 400 max_tokens_exceeded (BRIEF L54, L144; EXC1 L16). 'Accuracy drops as irrelevant content grows' [vendor] (BRIEF L73, L365); 'nobody has quantified accuracy lost per kilobyte of irrelevant state' (EXC2 L43). jgrep 'weak on long inputs' and truncates at 8,000 chars; foreman caps at 12k (EXC1 L61; EXC2 L32). semantic-find scores 218 line ids in one request [vendor] (EXC2 L7); batching 13 questions 12.2x cheaper/10x faster [vendor] (EXC2 L23); jgrep latency flat 1-64 questions (EXC1 L61). Fixture HTML up to 201,904 bytes (SCOUT L12).

findings.claim: Cost is negligible but latency is incompatible with Defuddle's synchronous browser API; only the async Node/Worker paths could call Jev, and the Worker could use the Cloudflare Workers AI binding (jev-1.13.0, ZDR).
findings.evidence: $0.042/M input, output free; 447-token 3-question call ~ $0.000019 (BRIEF L149; EXC1 L18) -> ~$0.0004 per 10k-token page if the shared state is billed once (inference from vendor '12.2x cheaper' batching claim). Latency: p50 126.81-175 ms direct short; p95 270 / p99 353 ms at 2,605 tokens; 315-524 ms with a few k tokens or one gateway; 580-800 ms two hops; 'under 100 ms' press claim unsupported (EXC1 L55-56). Browser parse() is synchronous (SCOUT L10). Workers AI env.AI.run('typesafe/jev') returns jev-1.13.0, ZDR 'Yes', $0.042 (BRIEF L303; EXC1 L21). Defuddle Worker charges $0.003-0.005/request (SCOUT L6).

findings.claim: Availability is fragile: direct signups paused, rate limits are the CEO's stated 'main worry', 429/529 are expected, and there is no browser-safe mode (a shipped key is exposed), so the browser extension cannot call Jev directly.
findings.evidence: Signups paused Sept 22; $5 credit ~120M tokens (BRIEF L57; EXC1 L17). Community-cited limits 250,000 tokens/s and 1,200 req/min; 429/529 retried by SDKs (BRIEF L147-148). Official SDKs Python/JS only (BRIEF L189). jev4k README: key exposed in a browser (EXC1 L24). Defuddle: zero deps, 92 KB gzip budget (SCOUT L9).

findings.claim: Privacy facts exclude the browser extension path and complicate the Worker path: US hosting, ZDR only for enterprise, an Oct 24 2026 leak of every customer's Noul outputs, and Defuddle's own promise that the npm package and extension make no network requests while running on logged-in pages.
findings.evidence: No training on user data; ZDR via enterprise sales; US-hosted (BRIEF L151, L387; EXC1 L22). Oct 24 leak disclosed by CEO, no postmortem, IDOR-class inferred (EXC1 L22; BRIEF L385). Attribute inference 100% from labels alone (EXC1 L46). Gateway ZDR: Workers AI 'Yes', Vercel per-request flags (BRIEF L296, L303). privacy.ts promise and Gmail extractor (SCOUT L8, L42).

findings.claim: Every precedent that judges DOM elements or web content publishes no accuracy number; the only measured web-page outcomes in the docs are failures.
findings.evidence: typesafe-adblock (81 stars): 'No accuracy figures published' (EXC2 L5); unclutter, Hide posts on X, Doomscroll Filter: 'no measured accuracy' (EXC2 L6); jev-ultrafast: 'three repeats of one task, not a reliability benchmark', 91% ad click (EXC2 L4); no WebArena/OSWorld score for any harness (EXC2 L13); guessed threshold threw away a third of good pages (EXC2 L39); pi-warden relevance compaction kept 1 of 34 files and did not ship (EXC2 L16). Positive vendor demos only: semantic-find 218 line ids, RAG cookbook 'a filter, not a security boundary' (EXC2 L7-8).

findings.claim: Jev is not uniquely capable: open models at or above ~4B parameters match or beat it on the same wire protocol, including options deployable on Workers AI or locally, while sub-500M encoders are useless zero-shot but become useful if fine-tuned in-domain (which Defuddle's 226 expected outputs could seed).
findings.evidence: JevBench ranks Jev 1.13 #26, 1.14 #31; Decision Index #43; untuned Gemma 4 31B 79.6 vs Jev 80.1 (BRIEF L393, L406; EXC1 L10). H2O-Lightning-4B Apache-2.0, 29 ms/decision, beats 1.13 (EXC2 L52). Clef on Workers AI @cf/cloudflare/clef $0.24/M; pplx-decider $0.02/M, 'best calibration among hosted' [vendor]; Ollaya local ECE 0.022 vs raw softmax 0.115 but 314 ms-62 s on CPU (EXC2 L51-52). Laya 421M / GLiNER2.5 340M ~0 chance-corrected zero-shot; Laya fine-tuned 0.362->0.766 and 44%->69%; 33 ms T4, 7.2 ms batched; laya-ts/receptron/edgejev/SemIf WebGPU exist (EXC2 L53). Quantization below Q8 costs 1-4 pts (EXC2 L54). Together $17/25-min Qwen3.5-4B fine-tune (EXC2 L45).

findings.claim: Strongest PRO-Jev evidence for clutter classification: Defuddle's known false positives are semantic misreads of prose (navigation words inside paragraphs), which is exactly the text-readable judgment where Jev is within 3 points of frontier LLMs at ~$0.0004/page, dozens of block questions per call are near-free, and thresholds can be tuned from Defuddle's existing labeled outputs.
findings.evidence: Scoring removes prose that merely contains words like 'privacy'/'share' (#112) and hand-maintained word/regex lists (SCOUT L33, L47). Jev-as-judge within 3 pts where verdict readable (EXC1 L59); spam F1 0.91, AG News 86.6% (EXC1 L61); 97.0% retained with option-wise Nouls at 0.90 (BRIEF L326); 10-label tuning +8.7 F1 (EXC1 L60); batching 218 questions over one state [vendor] (EXC2 L7); 'model output never becomes selectors' pattern in jev-ultrafast matches Defuddle's code-owns-candidates architecture (EXC2 L4); Workers AI ZDR binding (BRIEF L303).

findings.claim: Strongest ANTI evidence: many of Defuddle's removal decisions depend on facts not literally present in block text (hidden styles, image pixel size, link density, position relative to h1, word counts), which the docs say Jev cannot compute or simulate; those facts would have to be precomputed in code, which is what the existing pipeline already does.
findings.evidence: 'Jev evaluates what is in the state; it does not simulate what is absent' (EXC2 L34); counting/arithmetic collapse: MathQA 17.7 pts below, numeric packet features 28.42% vs RF 69.95% (BRIEF L362; EXC2 L25); 'Nothing numeric, temporal, or counted is left for the model to compute' checklist (BRIEF L416); compute-facts-then-judge gains chess 35%->5-9% (BRIEF L346). Defuddle steps 5-6 and 9 use measured sizes, computed styles, link density and word counts (SCOUT L29-33).

findings.claim: Vendor-origin facts in the docs that should not be treated as independent measurements: pricing ($0.042/M, no pricing page, possibly subsidized), the 193.6x/444.6x speed-cost multipliers, 'under 100 ms', the 12.2x-cheaper batching claim, the confidence formulas and 0.7/0.3 and >=0.9/0.5 thresholds, the jaggedness failure list, the no-training/ZDR/US-hosting policy, context limits and the '262k is slower and less accurate' admission, 30/60-day deprecation promises, Workers AI ZDR 'Yes' and Clef/pplx-decider/H2O/Torchcast/Together numbers (third-party vendors), the semantic-find/RAG/citation/reranking cookbook results, 1.14's 'subtle improvements', and first-option bias.
findings.evidence: Flags: EXC1 L9 ('193.6x faster, 444.6x cheaper' from vendor workflows vs LLM consensus labels; user medians 7x/30x); EXC1 L18 ('cannot prove pricing is not subsidized'); BRIEF L12 and EXC1 L56 ('under 100 ms' not supported by any independent measurement); EXC2 L23 ([vendor] batching); BRIEF L169-173, L183 (confidence page, concept page); BRIEF L357 (jaggedness list, 'each confirmed in the field'); BRIEF L151 (legal page); BRIEF L54, L144 (models page); BRIEF L161; BRIEF L303, L399-405; EXC2 L7-9; BRIEF L160, L368 [vendor]. Rate-limit figures (250k tokens/s, 1,200 rpm) are community-cited, not vendor-published (BRIEF L147).

caveats: All numbers come from three condensed documents prepared by others; I did not verify primary sources and made no API calls, so transcription errors upstream would propagate.

Many figures are from community blog posts or READMEs with tiny samples (Every n=7, MindStudio n=8, nexibeo 16-36 items, jev-ultrafast 'three repeats of one task'); only Deusser (346,009 requests), OpenRouter Banking77 (3,080), pi-warden (15,346 / 18,075), Guo (44 benchmarks) and jgrep (5,574 / 7,600) are large.

The 12% chosen-option flip rate (Yang et al.) was measured on hard game-theory style tasks; jgrep's 128/150 identical reruns with <=0.03 movement suggests flips are far rarer on confident, text-readable decisions. The true flip rate for near-threshold DOM blocks is unmeasured.

The 5.6% error at probability 1.0 (Du et al.) is from medical diagnosis (DDXPlus), not text-readable classification, and may overstate the error at p=1 on easy tasks; it is still the only published number for that band.

Page-level arithmetic assumes independent per-block errors and 10-100 candidate blocks per page; real block errors are correlated and Defuddle's per-page block count is unknown (fixtures are mostly small hand-made cases, SCOUT L12).

The 'what a keep-this-block Noul could reach' band (85-92% raw; 96-99% in the high-confidence band) is inference by analogy from spam/news/relevance tasks, not a measurement on DOM blocks; no document contains any DOM-element accuracy figure.

Per-page cost (~$0.0004 at 10k tokens) assumes the shared state is billed once per request regardless of question count; this is inferred from the vendor's '12.2x cheaper' batching claim and jgrep's flat latency, not from a published billing rule.
The '3-6 points below frontier LLMs' figure is the brief author's synthesis across independent studies, not a single measurement.
The version-drift observation (confidence 1.0 on 1.13.0 vs 0.99 on 1.14.0) comes from pre-existing local smoke files (n=1) produced by the orchestrator, not from the documents.

Vendor claims were flagged from the documents' own [vendor] markers plus source attribution (TypeSafe docs/cookbooks, Cloudflare/Perplexity/H2O/Together pages); some third-party-vendor numbers (e.g., H2O-Lightning beating Jev) are corroborated by public leaderboards.

metrics.smoke_version_drift_local_n1: same 453-token state: 1.13.0 confidence 1.0 / navigation 1.0; 1.14.0 confidence 0.99 / navigation 0.99, promo 0.01

result.verdict_for_this_dimension: The documents contain no evidence that Jev can make either meaning of Defuddle "sanitization" ~99.99% reliable. For deterministic security sanitization (A) the docs are unanimous and prohibitive: state is "argued input", injection succeeds 93.5-100% of the time, guards fail open 93-100% under misleading labels, confidence is not authorization, and the recommended design is a deterministic validator the model cannot override, which Defuddle already has. For heuristic clutter removal (B) the best analogous measurements put a zero-shot "keep this block?" Noul at roughly 85-92% per block, ~93-97% after threshold tuning on Defuddle's labeled fixtures, and ~96-99% inside a high-confidence band covering ~58-76% of blocks; even the p=1.0 band carries 5.6% error in one study, outputs flip on ~12% of repeats with no seeds and 30-day version deprecation, and no DOM-element precedent publishes any accuracy. Compounded over tens of blocks per page, 99%-per-block yields ~60% fully-correct pages and 99.99% page-level would need 99.9998% per block, two to three orders of magnitude beyond any number in the docs. The evidence therefore supports, at most, a cautious use: an asynchronous, version-pinned, cached, shadow-mode, threshold-tuned tie-breaker for ambiguous blocks in the Node/Worker paths (Workers AI binding with ZDR), with the deterministic sanitizer and the existing heuristics retained as the decision of record. Aggressive use is contradicted by every production precedent, and the browser-extension path is excluded by the synchronous API, the no-network privacy promise, key exposure, and the Oct 24 output leak.

result.title: Jev document evidence extraction: what the docs say about reaching ~99.99% reliable HTML "sanitization" in Defuddle
result.summary:
I read the five shared files in full (SCOUT_NOTES, EXPERIMENT_RULES, JEV_AGENT_BRIEF 437 lines, JEV_ECOSYSTEM_EXCERPTS_1 67 lines, JEV_ECOSYSTEM_EXCERPTS_2 57 lines), made no API calls and read no repo code, and extracted 114 evidence rows (claim, number, source, vendor-vs-independent, file+line) across topics (a)-(k) into /tmp/jev-research/results/doc-evidence-v2/evidence_table.md. I then ran a small script (page_level_math.py) that turns the per-decision numbers in the docs into page-level, fixture-suite and cost arithmetic; those derived numbers are inference under an independence assumption and are labelled as such.

Measured facts on accuracy: the best per-decision figures anywhere in the docs are 95-99% on the easiest sentiment/NLI benchmarks (Deusser, independent), 96.3% in the confidence>=0.99 band on Banking77 (covers 58% of items; OpenRouter), 97.0% for option-wise Nouls at a 0.90 threshold (Du et al.), and a self-reported "under 1%" error rate above confidence 0.8 on 15,346 production tool-call judgments (pi-warden, coverage of that band not stated). Even decisions returned at probability exactly 1.0 were wrong 5.6% of the time in one medical study (102/1,819). The closest analogues to a "keep this block?" Noul are binary text filters: spam F1 0.91, AG News 86.6%, search-result relevance 74%, Jev-as-a-Judge "within 3 points of GPT-6 where the verdict can be read from the text". Every DOM/web precedent (typesafe-adblock, unclutter, Hide-posts-on-X, semantic-find, jev-ultrafast node picking, RAG filter) publishes no accuracy number at all; the only measured web-page outcomes are negative (jev-ultrafast clicked a planted ad 91% of the time; a guessed threshold "threw away a third of the good pages"; pi-warden's relevance compaction kept 1 of 34 files and was dropped). By analogy I would expect a well-written, threshold-tuned per-block Noul to land around 85-92% zero-shot overall and 96-99% inside a high-confidence band covering roughly half to three-quarters of blocks; that is inference, not measurement.

Reliability-in-the-engineering-sense facts: Jev has no seeds; the chosen option changes on 12% of repeats and probabilities move ~0.04 (Yang et al.); jgrep saw 128/150 questions identical across three runs; jev-latest drifts and pinned versions carry only a 30-day deprecation promise; the vendor's only reproducibility path is a cache keyed on (model, state, questions). Defuddle's 226-fixture suite requires byte-equal Markdown with the network disabled, so any live Jev step would make the suite non-reproducible (at a 12% per-decision flip rate the probability that all 226 fixtures stay identical is ~1e-126 even at 10 decisions per fixture; even at a 0.1% cross-threshold flip rate ~11 fixtures would fail per run at 50 decisions each). Security facts are unambiguous and all independent: injection in the state drives routing accuracy from 100% to 0-5.8% (ASR 93.5-100%), one appended opinion flips 12.1% of decisions, natural context flips 61-73%, attacked decisions keep their confidence ("confidence is not authorization"), a TokenBreak respelling bypassed a toxicity filter that caught 30/30 unedited prompts, and the report's conclusion is that Jev treats its state as "argued input" and must never be the sole gate; a deterministic validator the model cannot override is the consensus pattern. Context is 32k tokens per question / 64k per request (262k mode is "slower and less accurate"), accuracy drops with irrelevant state and "nobody has quantified accuracy lost per kilobyte", while Defuddle's largest fixture alone is 202 KB of HTML. Price is $0.042/M input (about $0.0002 per 5k-token page, 7% of defuddle.md's $0.003 price), latency 100-500 ms direct, 524 ms median measured from Cloudflare, 500-800 ms through two hops; signups have been paused since Sept 22; data is US-hosted with ZDR only via enterprise sales, and an Oct 24 leak exposed every customer's Noul outputs. Official SDKs are Python/JS only, there is no browser-safe mode (a shipped key is exposed), and the Workers AI binding returns jev-1.13.0 with ZDR "Yes".

Implication for the Jev question: the documents contain no number within two orders of magnitude of 99.99% per decision (the target is 1 error per 10,000; the best independent high-confidence band is 370 per 10,000 and the best self-reported figure is <100 per 10,000), and compounding across tens of block decisions per page pushes page-level correctness far lower (99% per block gives 60% fully-correct pages at 50 blocks; 99.99% page-level at 50 blocks would need 99.9998% per block). For meaning A (security sanitization) the docs' own non-negotiable rules exclude Jev as a gate. For meaning B (clutter removal) the strongest supportable use is a confidence-gated, cached, shadow-tested advisory signal on the uncertain middle band of the existing heuristics, in Node/Worker environments only, with the deterministic pipeline unchanged; aggressive use is contradicted by the non-determinism, context, argued-input, privacy and browser-key facts.

findings.claim: No number in the three Jev documents comes within two orders of magnitude of 99.99% per decision; the best independent high-confidence band is 96.3% and the best self-reported production band is 'under 1%' error.
findings.evidence: Banking77 confidence>=0.99 band: 58% coverage at 96.3% accuracy (EXC1 L66; BRIEF L179). pi-warden: 15,346 judged tool calls, wrong 15% below confidence 0.8 and under 1% above, band coverage not stated (EXC1 L67; EXC2 L16). Option-wise Nouls at 0.90 threshold retain 97.0% vs Choice 79.4% (BRIEF L326). Du et al.: 1,819 decisions at p=1.0 included 102 errors = 5.6% (EXC1 L33). Easiest benchmarks top out at 95-99% (IMDB/SST-2/HellaSwag/ARC, EXC1 L8). 99.99% = 1 error/10k; 96.3% = 370/10k; 99% = 100/10k.

findings.claim: The closest measured analogues to a 'keep this block?' Noul are binary/few-class text filters scoring 74-91%, which by analogy puts a zero-shot per-block Noul around 85-92% overall and 96-99% only inside a high-confidence band (inference).
findings.evidence: jgrep SMS spam one-Noul-per-line F1 0.91 (P 0.87/R 0.95, 5,574 msgs); AG News 86.6% zero-shot with business-class precision 0.58 (EXC1 L61). Distil Labs relevance on 2,380 labeled results: Jev 74% (EXC1 L65). Jev-as-a-Judge within 3 points of GPT-6 'where the verdict can be read from the text' (EXC1 L59). Noul soft accuracy 0.918 is the best-calibrated primitive (EXC1 L29). Threshold tuning on 10 labels lifted F1 0.706->0.793 (EXC1 L60); decomposition into 5 questions + LR on 1,000 labels lifted phishing 62.6%->95.0% (EXC1 L62). Block classification has ambiguous categories (bios, related posts, captions, comments) that resemble the weak rubric end (Emotion 0.585, EXC1 L8) more than sentiment.

findings.claim: Page-level compounding makes the gap worse: with tens of block decisions per page, even 99% per block yields only ~60% fully-correct pages at 50 blocks, and 99.99% page-level correctness at 50 blocks would require 99.9998% per block (derived, independence assumed).
findings.evidence: Computed in /tmp/jev-research/results/doc-evidence-v2/page_level_math.py from doc numbers: P(all 50 correct) = 0.963^50 = 0.152; 0.99^50 = 0.605; 0.999^50 = 0.951; required per-block accuracy for page target 0.9999 at N=50 = 0.999998. Expected errors per 50-block page: 1.85 at 96.3%, 0.5 at 99%.

findings.claim: Jev is non-deterministic with no seed, which is incompatible with Defuddle's byte-exact, network-disabled 226-fixture suite unless every decision is recorded and replayed from a committed cache.
findings.evidence: Yang et al.: 0.04 average probability movement and 12% chosen-option change on repeats (EXC1 L20, L49; BRIEF L150). jgrep: 128/150 questions identical over three uncached runs (EXC1 L20). OpenRouter: Score 1.21 then 1.17, Noul 0.42 then 0.44 on the same message (EXC1 L20). No seeds; jev-latest changes (EXC2 L46; BRIEF L72). Only deterministic path: cache keyed on (model, state, questions) (BRIEF L332). Pinned-version deprecation notice shrank from 60 to 30 days (BRIEF L161). Workspace smoke files show jev-1.13.0 returning confidence 1.0 and jev-1.14.0 returning 0.99 on the identical 453-token state. Derived: at a 12% flip rate P(all 226 fixtures identical) ~ 3e-126 at 10 decisions/fixture; at 0.1% ~11 of 226 fixtures fail per run at 50 decisions/fixture. SCOUT L11: fixture tests are hermetic with network disabled.

findings.claim: For security sanitization (SCOUT meaning A), the docs' own rules exclude Jev: it is 'never the only gate', state is 'argued input', confidence is not authorization, and a deterministic validator the model cannot override is mandatory.
findings.evidence: Wang et al.: routing accuracy 100% clean -> 0-5.8% under injection, ASR 93.5-100% on the official API (EXC1 L41; BRIEF L33). JevAdvBench: one appended opinion flips 12.1% of decisions and pushes 38% of confident answers below 0.8 (EXC1 L42). JevOut: 61.4-73.2% of correct decisions redirected by natural context (EXC1 L43). Azizi: typed-model guardrails failed open 93-100% under a misleading option label while one deterministic rule reached 100% (BRIEF L382). 'Attacked decisions were as confident as the originals' (BRIEF L383). HiddenLayer: toxicity filter caught 30/30 unedited prompts but 'many' TokenBreak-respelled ones passed (EXC1 L45). Conclusion quoted: 'Anyone who wires Jev into a security boundary is wiring in a model that treats its state as argued input' (EXC1 L11). All of these are independent measurements.

findings.claim: For clutter removal (meaning B) the argued-input weakness is still material because the adversary is the page author/ad network: the one measured DOM-level case shows a Jev harness choosing a planted ad 91% of the time despite an explicit 'page text is untrusted' instruction.
findings.evidence: HiddenLayer on browser-use/jev-ultrafast: clicked a planted 'Confirm Price' ad 91% of the time (EXC1 L44; EXC2 L4). JevAdvBench 12.1% flip from one appended opinion (EXC1 L42). TokenBreak respelling bypass (EXC1 L45) shows filters are gameable by adaptive text changes. Defuddle's existing regex selectors are also gameable, but deterministically and auditable; Jev returns no reasons (EXC2 L44, L18).

findings.claim: Calibration supports a three-band cascade (auto / cautious / fall back) but only after per-task threshold tuning; the 0.5 default is wrong, per-task ECE is poor, and the cascade gain over a single system is bounded.
findings.evidence: Median F1-optimal Noul threshold 0.35 across 31 benchmarks (BRIEF L177; EXC1 L47). Pooled ECE 0.047 but median per-benchmark ECE 0.168, range 0.003-0.28 (BRIEF L180). Noul has no confidence field; docs suggest |2p-1| with 0.7/0.3 starting thresholds; worked examples use >=0.9 for high-stakes auto-actions and a 0.5 floor for human routing (BRIEF L173, L183; vendor guidance). Banking77 cascade at 0.90: Jev handles 75.9%, 84.0% overall vs Opus 84.4% at ~28% cost (EXC1 L66). Rao & Callison-Burch: flash-tier LLM judges repeat >85% of Jev's most confident errors; cascades gain <=2.7 points even with oracle thresholds (EXC1 L52). In-sample thresholds targeting 5% FNR miss up to 17% held-out (EXC2 L19). Coherence: P(X)+P(not X) misses 1 by 0.064 (EXC1 L48). Derived: with the Banking77 bands, overall accuracy = 0.58*0.963 + 0.42*h, i.e. 93.7% if the fallback heuristics are 90% accurate on the hard remainder, 97.4% if they are 99%.

findings.claim: Context limits force a lossy pre-reduction of real pages before Jev can see them, and the accuracy cost of irrelevant state is unquantified; the recommended pattern is one shared page state with many per-block Nouls (batch questions, not items).
findings.evidence: 32k tokens per question (state + question), 64k per request; 262k only with the Danger-Zone-Long-Context header and 'slower and less accurate'; 400 max_tokens_exceeded (BRIEF L54, L144; EXC1 L16). 'Accuracy drops as irrelevant content grows' (BRIEF L73, vendor-disclosed) and 'nobody has quantified accuracy lost per kilobyte of irrelevant state' (EXC2 L43). Batching: 13 questions in one call 12.2x cheaper/10x faster with identical answers (vendor cookbook, BRIEF L344); jgrep latency flat from 1 to 64 questions (EXC1 L61); semantic-find scored 218 line-id Nouls over one shared state (EXC2 L7, vendor). Field truncation: jgrep cuts records at 8,000 chars, foreman at 12k (EXC2 L32). Defuddle fixture HTML max 201,904 bytes, p90 8,788 (SCOUT L12); 200 KB of HTML is well over 32k tokens, so the state must be a stripped text/outline representation, itself a heuristic step.

findings.claim: Cost is negligible relative to defuddle.md pricing but latency is 2-3 orders of magnitude above the local pipeline, and direct access is currently gated by paused signups and org rate limits.
findings.evidence: $0.042/M input, output free, same for 1.13 and 1.14 (BRIEF L149; vendor price confirmed by gateway listings). Derived: a 5k-token page state ~ $0.00021 = 7% of defuddle.md's $0.003 request price; a 32k-token state ~ $0.0013 = 45%. Latency: LiteLLM p50 126.81 ms; OpenRouter p50 175/p95 270/p99 353 ms at 2,605 mean tokens; Jev-IDS 315-335 ms at ~1.8k tokens; Cloudflare-measured 524 ms median; jev-guard ~580 ms p50 via AI Gateway, ~0.75 s from Taiwan; 'under 100 ms' press claim unsupported (EXC1 L55-56). Rate limits per org, community cites 250,000 tokens/s and 1,200 req/min; CEO calls rate limits 'the main worry'; direct signups paused Sept 22 (BRIEF L57, L147; EXC1 L17).

findings.claim: Privacy and hosting facts conflict with Defuddle's published 'no network requests' promise for the npm package and browser extension; only the Worker could plausibly call Jev, via the Workers AI binding with ZDR.
findings.evidence: US-hosted; 'commitment not to train'; ZDR only for enterprise via sales (BRIEF L151, L387; EXC1 L22; vendor claims). Oct 24, 2026: CEO disclosed a leak exposing every customer's Noul outputs, no postmortem, IDOR-class bug inferred (EXC1 L22; press). Cloudflare Workers AI: env.AI.run('typesafe/jev'), ZDR 'Yes', returns jev-1.13.0 (BRIEF L303; gateway claim). Vercel gateway has per-request ZDR/no-training flags (BRIEF L296). Attribute inference: 100% accuracy for gender/age/health/ethnicity from labels alone (EXC1 L46). SCOUT L8: 'The npm package and browser extension run entirely locally and make no network requests'; SCOUT L42: the extension runs on logged-in pages and a Gmail extractor exists.

findings.claim: Runtime availability excludes the primary browser environment: official SDKs are Python and JS (Node 20+) only, there is no browser-safe mode, and sub-500M on-device encoders that could run in a browser score near zero zero-shot.
findings.evidence: SDKs: Python 3.10+ and JS Node 20+; everything else calls HTTP (BRIEF L189). 'No browser-safe mode: a key shipped in client code is exposed' (EXC1 L24). Gateways (Vercel, Netlify, OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Workers AI) need no TypeSafe key but still run server-side (BRIEF L277-308). On-device: laya-ts, receptron/laya ONNX, edgejev, SemIf WebGPU exist; Laya 33 ms on a T4; but 340M-421M encoders score ~0 on chance-corrected indices unless fine-tuned in-domain and the floor for Jev-level quality is ~4B parameters (EXC2 L53; BRIEF L408), far beyond Defuddle's 92 KB gzip bundle budget (SCOUT L9).

findings.claim: Every existing DOM/web-content precedent publishes no accuracy figure; the only quantified web outcomes in the docs are failures.
findings.evidence: typesafe-adblock: 81 stars, 3,872-like demo, 'No accuracy figures published' (EXC2 L5). unclutter 304 stars, Hide posts on X, Doomscroll Filter, X algorithm rebuilt: 'no measured accuracy' (EXC2 L6). jev-ultrafast: 23.7k stars, 3 commits, 1 contributor, 'three repeats of one task, not a reliability benchmark', model output never becomes selectors, 91% planted-ad click (EXC2 L4). semantic-find: 218 line Nouls, vendor cookbook, no accuracy (EXC2 L7). RAG filter: 'a filter, not a security boundary' (EXC2 L8). No WebArena/OSWorld score for any Jev harness (EXC2 L13). pi-warden relevance compaction kept 1 of 34 files and did not ship (EXC2 L16). 'I Guessed My Jev Threshold. It Threw Away a Third of the Good Pages' (EXC2 L39).

findings.claim: Offline/privacy alternatives on the same wire protocol exist for Node/CLI/Worker (Ollaya, H2O-Lightning-4B, Winnow-12B, Clef on Workers AI, pplx-decider), but all sit at or above ~4B parameters and none is in-browser or inside a 92 KB bundle; quality claims for them are mostly their own vendors'.
findings.evidence: Ollaya: Rust daemon, /v1/systemone, ~25 families, author-calibrated ECE 0.022 vs raw softmax 0.115, 14 ms-1.0 s on RTX 5090 but 314 ms-62 s on CPU (EXC2 L51; author-reported). H2O-Lightning-4B Apache-2.0, 29 ms, 'beats Jev 1.13 on JevBench' (H2O claim, EXC2 L52). Winnow-12B Apache-2.0 ~61k HF downloads/month; Kev 8.4k stars (EXC2 L52). Clef on Workers AI @cf/cloudflare/clef, $0.24/M, Apache-2.0 (Cloudflare claim, BRIEF L399). pplx-decider $0.02/M, rank 5 on Decision Index (BRIEF L400). AnyJev: untuned Gemma 4 31B 79.6 vs Jev 80.1 (independent, BRIEF L406). Laya 421M / GLiNER2.5-Decide 340M ~0 zero-shot, rescued only by in-domain fine-tuning 0.362->0.766 (EXC2 L53). Quantization below Q8 costs 1-4 points; Ollama raw softmax discards calibration (EXC2 L54). Fine-tuning Jev itself is impossible; a Qwen3.5-4B fine-tune cost $17/25 min at Together (EXC2 L45).

findings.claim: Strongest PRO-Jev evidence for clutter classification: it is a text-readable binary judgment, Noul is the best-calibrated primitive, high-confidence bands are reliable, question batching makes a per-block fan-out cheap, and the pattern 'code computes facts, Jev judges, code decides' fits Defuddle's scoring step (e.g. prose wrongly removed for containing navigation words).
findings.evidence: Jev-as-a-Judge within 3 points of GPT-6 where the verdict is readable from text (EXC1 L59); Noul soft accuracy 0.918 (EXC1 L29); spam F1 0.91 (EXC1 L61); conf>=0.99 band 96.3% on 58% (EXC1 L66); pi-warden <1% above 0.8 (EXC1 L67); option-wise Nouls 97.0% at 0.9 (BRIEF L326); 10-label tuning +8.7 F1 (EXC1 L60); 5-question decomposition 62.6->95% (EXC1 L62); 218 Nouls per request (EXC2 L7); latency flat 1-64 questions (EXC1 L61); ~$0.0002/page derived; Workers AI binding with ZDR (BRIEF L303); same wire protocol allows swapping to an open model (BRIEF L15); compute-facts gains (chess blunders 35%->5-9%, BRIEF L346). SCOUT L47 names the #112 class of error (scoring removes prose containing navigation words), which is a literal-text judgment.

findings.claim: Strongest ANTI evidence: no DOM precedent has a measured accuracy; non-determinism breaks the fixture contract; context limits force lossy pre-reduction; argued input is exploitable by page authors; the primary environment cannot hold a key or send content off-device; and the best measured band is ~100x short of 99.99%.
findings.evidence: EXC2 L5-6 (no accuracy), EXC1 L20/L49 (12% flips), BRIEF L144 (32k/64k), EXC2 L43 (unquantified irrelevant-state loss), EXC1 L41-44 (injection, 91% ad click), EXC1 L24 (no browser-safe mode), SCOUT L8 (no-network promise), EXC1 L22 (leak), EXC1 L52 (cascade <=2.7 pts), EXC2 L39 (third of good pages discarded), EXC2 L18 (~68% guard accuracy), EXC1 L33 (5.6% wrong at p=1.0).

findings.claim: Vendor claims that should not be treated as measurements: the 193.6x/444.6x multipliers, 'under 100 ms', 1.14's 'small, subtle improvements' and multilingual gain, every cookbook result (12.2x cheaper/10x faster, reranking 5%->18%, citation 4/4, semantic-find 218, RAG injection 0.99), the confidence formula and 0.7/0.3/0.9/0.5 threshold suggestions, the calibration disclaimer, the no-training and ZDR statements, and the deprecation promises; third-party vendor claims include Cloudflare's ZDR 'Yes' and Clef compatibility, Vercel's ZDR flags, H2O/Torchcast/Perplexity/Together figures for their own models, Distil Labs' Laya numbers, and Ollaya's ECE 0.022.
findings.evidence: EXC1 L9 (193.6x/444.6x 'from vendor-built workflows scored against LLM consensus labels'; user medians 7x/30x); EXC1 L56 ('under 100 ms' not supported by any independent measurement); BRIEF L160 ([vendor] quality note); EXC2 L23 (cookbooks marked [vendor]); BRIEF L169-183 (confidence page, concept page); EXC1 L19 (calibration disclaimer); BRIEF L151 (legal page); BRIEF L161 (deprecation); BRIEF L303, L296 (gateway pages); EXC2 L51-52 and EXC1 L65 (competitor figures). The vendor's own jaggedness list (BRIEF L357-375) is a self-disclosed limitation list that the brief says was 'each confirmed in the field'. Semi-independent: OpenRouter is a reseller but reports numbers unfavorable to Jev; pi-warden, jgrep and nexibeo are self-reported community measurements, not peer-reviewed.

findings.claim: Even the perfect-score community samples cannot support a 99.99% claim: the rule of three bounds the error rate of 40/40 at <7.5% and of 34/34 at <8.8% (95%), and the largest production log (15,346) reports ~1% errors rather than zero.
findings.evidence: nexibeo invoice 40/40, triage 34/34, moderation 0 errors on 16-36 items, four Nouls 7/7 (EXC2 L11). Rule-of-three computed in page_level_math.py: 3/40 = 0.075, 3/34 = 0.088, 3/7 = 0.43; 3/15,346 = 0.0002 would be the bound only if pi-warden had reported zero errors, which it did not (EXC1 L67).

caveats: All numbers are taken from condensed secondary documents (a brief and two excerpt files), not from the primary papers; line references point to those files, and I did not verify the primary sources.

Page-level, fixture-suite, cascade and cost arithmetic in /tmp/jev-research/results/doc-evidence-v2/ is my own inference under an independence assumption; real block errors on a page are correlated, which changes the numbers but not the orders of magnitude.
The 'keep this block?' accuracy range (85-92% zero-shot, 96-99% in a confident band) is analogy, not measurement; no document reports a measured accuracy for any DOM-element classification task.

The fixture-suite flip-rate calculation uses the 12% chosen-option change rate from Yang et al., which was measured on Choice questions across repeats; for thresholded Nouls only probability movements that cross the code threshold cause a flip, so the true rate on this task is unknown and could be much lower (I also show 1%, 0.1% and 0.01% scenarios).

pi-warden's '<1% above 0.8', jgrep's figures and nexibeo's recipes are self-reported community numbers from project READMEs, not peer-reviewed; OpenRouter is a reseller of Jev; the vendor-claim flags are as marked in the source documents plus my own classification of gateway and competitor statements.
Token counts for HTML pages (used for the cost table) assume roughly 3-4 characters per token; HTML markup is token-dense and the actual ratio was not measured here.

Cost arithmetic assumes the shared state is billed once per request when many questions are batched, consistent with the brief's '13 questions in one call 12.2x cheaper' vendor cookbook claim, which was not independently verified in the docs.

The smoke-test files in /tmp/jev-research (jev-1.13.0 confidence 1.0 vs jev-1.14.0 confidence 0.99 on the same state) are a single workspace observation included as an illustration of version drift, not part of the documents and not a measurement of drift rate.
Workers AI serves jev-1.13.0 while jev-latest is 1.14.0; any accuracy figure attributed to one version may not transfer to the other, and the docs describe 1.14's independent results as 'mixed'.
A prior run of this slice left files in /tmp/jev-research/results/doc-evidence/; I wrote fresh outputs to /tmp/jev-research/results/doc-evidence-v2/ and did not modify the earlier folder.

privacy.zdr: enterprise only (direct); Workers AI ZDR yes; Vercel per-request flag

result.verdict_for_this_dimension: The Jev documents do not support "~99.99% reliable". Measured per-decision reliability tops out at 95-99% on the easiest text benchmarks and 96.3-99% inside high-confidence bands (the 99% figure is self-reported with unstated coverage; decisions at probability 1.0 were still wrong 5.6% of the time in one study), i.e. 100-500 errors per 10,000 against a target of 1; the closest analogues to a per-block "keep?" Noul score 74-91%; no DOM-element precedent publishes any accuracy; and compounding across tens of blocks per page makes page-level correctness far lower still. Jev is also non-deterministic (12% option flips, no seeds, version drift), which is incompatible with Defuddle's byte-exact hermetic fixture suite except through a committed decision cache. For security sanitization (meaning A) the docs' own non-negotiable rules exclude Jev as a gate (93-100% injection ASR, "argued input", "never the sole gate", "confidence is not authorization"), so the deterministic sanitizer must stay unconditional. For clutter removal (meaning B) the evidence supports, at most, a cached, version-pinned, shadow-tested, confidence-gated advisory signal on the uncertain middle band of the existing heuristics, usable only in Node/CLI/Worker (no browser-safe key; US hosting, enterprise-only ZDR and an Oct 24 output leak conflict with the extension's "no network requests" promise), with an open same-wire model as the offline fallback. Aggressive use is contradicted by the determinism, context-limit, argued-input, privacy and runtime facts.

result.title: exp-main-container: Jev (jev-1.14.0) vs defuddle findMainContent at picking the main article container on 167 fixtures
result.summary:
What I did. A prior run of this slice had built the candidate set and collected four live Jev variants but never analyzed them or reported; "try again" was the re-launch. I re-ran the offline candidate build into a scratch directory and confirmed it is byte-identical to the stored /tmp/jev-research/results/exp-main-container/candidates.jsonl (so the stored Jev results are valid), ran the analysis, audited every ground-truth label, added one new live variant D (same as A but with every tag/id/class hint removed from the candidate descriptions, to test whether Jev reads content or the word "article"), computed order-rotation ensembles and confidence-gated cascades offline, and ran an end-to-end check that swaps each Jev pick into Defuddle as `contentSelector` and compares the Markdown to tests/expected exactly as tests/fixtures.test.ts does (my harness port reproduces 167/167 on the default pipeline). Candidates = ENTRY_POINT_ELEMENTS matches (src/constants.ts:3-24) with >=30 words, document order, truth = smallest candidate covering >=90% of the output's 5-word shingles (with a word-multiset fallback the previous builder added; 123 labels come from strict shingles, 39 from the fallback). Of 226 fixtures: 17 skipped (extractorType set), 42 skipped (<2 candidates), 167 kept; 126 have exactly 2 candidates (almost all body > article/main with identical text), 35 have 3, 6 have 4-10; only 9 are real full pages >20KB and 15 are >8KB; median kept fixture is ~1.7KB synthetic HTML. Total live spend across all five variants: 833 calls, 942,123 input tokens, about $0.040, zero HTTP errors, zero 400 max_tokens_exceeded (the two pages over the 25k-token cap for variant C were excluded, not sent).

What I found (measured). Variant A (JSON candidate list, document order, one Choice + 2 Nouls per candidate, model jev-1.14.0): 157/167 = 94.0% on the spec labels; after relabelling five provable label artifacts (footnote markers rewritten to `[^1]` and math rewritten to LaTeX drop word coverage to 0.82-0.87 although `c2` is the only article element and Jev picked it at 0.92-0.97) and accepting article-or-article-body on one ambiguous fixture, 163/167 = 97.6%. defuddle's own findMainContent pick equals the same adjudicated label 159/167 = 95.2%; on the 41 pages with >=3 nested candidates both score 37/41 (90.2%); on the 9 real pages Jev 9/9, findMainContent 7/9 (but defuddle's final output is still correct there via retries). Every adjudicated Jev-A miss sits at confidence <0.5 (band accuracy: >=0.9 112/112, 0.7-0.9 29/29, 0.5-0.7 11/11, <0.5 11/15). End-to-end: swapping Jev-A's raw pick into Defuddle passes 164/167 fixtures (98.2%); gating at confidence >=0.5 and falling back to findMainContent passes 167/167, as does full-page variant C (8 fall back on none_of_these). The two harmful raw misses are under-inclusion on a blog index (picked one card: 51 words out vs 172) and over-inclusion of a clutter-filled <main> when the real article was 57 words (623 words out vs 77) at confidence 0.45; a third raw e2e failure (GitHub issue) is a case where Jev matched the label but the label is wrong (even the oracle pick fails e2e because GitHub's "## Description" heading lives outside the inner markdown-body).

Sensitivity and what drives the answers. Reversing candidate order (variant B) flipped the argmax on 16/167 = 9.6% of pages and dropped accuracy to 150/167 adjudicated (26/41 = 63.4% on 3+ candidate pages), with 17 over-inclusive picks: Jev shifts toward whichever nested wrapper is listed last, so averaging A and B probabilities does not help (96.4%, below A alone). Exact repeat (A2) flipped 5/167 = 3.0%, all at confidence <=0.35, mean |delta p| 0.016. Removing tag/id/class hints (variant D) cut adjudicated accuracy from 97.6% to 88.0%, mean confidence from 0.85 to 0.49, and left zero picks at >=0.9 confidence: roughly ten points of accuracy and most of the confidence come from reading the same semantic names ("article", "main", "entry-content") that ENTRY_POINT_ELEMENTS already encodes deterministically; on near-identical nested candidates the remaining cue is the word count, which Jev compares poorly. Whole-page HTML (variant C, mean 1,580 tokens/page) scored 155/165 adjudicated with six low-confidence none_of_these abstentions on small synthetic pages, but it fixed the two content-blind misses of A (card grid, js-article-content) because it could see the clutter. The spec's Noul-derived pick (smallest with contains_all>=0.5 and non_article<=0.5) reached only 85.0% adjudicated with 23 abstentions: contains_all separates containers that hold the article from those that do not with AUROC 0.991, but non_article separates a clutter-bearing ancestor from the true container at only AUROC 0.834, because 300/150-character excerpts rarely show the clutter; loosening to contains_all>=0.3 gives 94.0%.

Implication for the Jev question. On this slice Jev is roughly a peer of findMainContent at naming the smallest covering container, and a confidence-gated Jev with findMainContent as fallback reproduces every expected output, but that parity is inherited from defuddle (the fallback and the downstream removal pipeline, which turns most over-inclusive picks into identical output). Nothing here points toward 99.99%: raw error is 2.4% on labels and 1.8% end-to-end, order sensitivity is 9.6% on exactly the nested-wrapper pages where a second opinion would matter, and the model's confidence is largely a restatement of the tag heuristics defuddle already has. The defensible use is narrow: a shadow or tie-break signal, gated at confidence >=0.5 (or >=0.7 for safety), on the roughly one quarter of pages that have three or more nested candidates, with full-page context when the page fits in budget, and never as the sole selector.

findings.claim: Jev-A (jev-1.14.0, candidate list, document order) names the smallest covering container 157/167 (94.0%) on the spec labels and 163/167 (97.6%) after adjudicating 6 noisy labels; defuddle's findMainContent names it 153/167 (91.6%) / 159/167 (95.2%) on the same labels.
findings.evidence: analysis.json variant_A.all_167_spec_labels.correct=157; analysis2.json accuracy.A.adjudicated_all=163/167, defuddle_findMainContent.strict_all=153, adjudicated_all=159. Adjudication: 5 'none_of_these' labels are artifacts (expected .md rewrites footnote markers to [^1] and math to LaTeX; word coverage 0.82-0.87 for the sole article element c2, which Jev picked at 0.92-0.97); issues--header-with-subtitle-p accepts c2 (article incl. h1) or c3 (article-body).

findings.claim: End-to-end, swapping Jev-A's raw pick into Defuddle as contentSelector passes 164/167 fixture tests (98.2%); gated at confidence >=0.5 with findMainContent as fallback it passes 167/167, as does full-page variant C; baseline is 167/167.
findings.evidence: e2e_swap_results.json: baseline 167 pass; jev_A 164 pass (fails: entry-point--js-article-content 623 words out vs 77 expected; general--tailwind-hidden-blog-index 51 vs 172; general--github.com-issue-56 267 vs 271); jev_A_conf_ge_0_5_else_default 167 pass (15 fell back); jev_C 167 pass (8 fell back); jev_B 165; jev_D 165; jev_A2 166. Harness port reproduces tests/fixtures.test.ts comparison (normalizeMarkdownHtml from tests/helpers.ts).

findings.claim: All four adjudicated Jev-A misses occur at Choice confidence <0.5 (0.20, 0.24, 0.25, 0.45); the 152 picks at confidence >=0.5 are 152/152 correct on adjudicated labels.
findings.evidence: analysis2.json accuracy.A.adjudicated_by_band: >=0.9 112/112, 0.7-0.9 29/29, 0.5-0.7 11/11, <0.5 11/15. cascade_A 'conf>=0.5': routed 152 (91.0%), jev_accuracy_on_routed 100%, overall 164/167 (the 3 remaining misses are fallback findMainContent misses on labels, all of which still pass e2e).

findings.claim: Order sensitivity is large on this task: reversing candidate order flips the argmax on 16/167 pages (9.6%) and drops adjudicated accuracy to 150/167, with 17 over-inclusive picks and 63.4% accuracy on 3+-candidate pages; Jev shifts toward the wrapper listed last. Averaging A and B probabilities (rotation ensemble) scores 161/167, below A alone.
findings.evidence: analysis.json order_sensitivity_A_vs_B: choice_flips 16, flip_rate_pct 9.6, both_correct 143, either_correct 158, max |delta p| 0.76; variant_B miss_relation ancestor_of_truth 17; analysis2.json accuracy.B.adjudicated_3plus 26/41; ensemble_A+B adjudicated_all 161/167. Literature figure for reversal flips is 1.8% (JEV_ECOSYSTEM_EXCERPTS_1.md), so nested near-duplicate candidates are a hard case.

findings.claim: Repeat stability is good: an exact repeat (A2) changed the chosen option on 5/167 (3.0%), all at confidence <=0.35; mean absolute probability movement on the chosen option 0.016, max on any option 0.12.
findings.evidence: analysis.json repeat_stability_A_vs_A2: choice_flips 5, flips at A-confidence 0.24/0.20/0.25/0.25/0.27, mean_abs_dp_chosen 0.016, max_abs_dp_any_option 0.12. Lower than the ~12% repeat-change rate reported in the literature brief.

findings.claim: A substantial share of Jev's accuracy and most of its confidence come from reading tag/id/class names: removing them (variant D) drops adjudicated accuracy from 97.6% to 88.0% (2-candidate pages 100% -> 92.9%; 3+ pages 90.2% -> 73.2%), mean confidence from 0.848 to 0.492, and leaves zero picks at >=0.9 confidence. On the 9 real pages D is still 9/9.
findings.evidence: analysis2.json accuracy.D and D_vs_A: 19 flips vs A, 14 of them body chosen over the article/main element on pages where both candidates have identical excerpt text and differ only in word count; D picked body 18 times vs 4 in A. Noul AUROC for contains_all fell 0.991 -> 0.971, non_article ancestor-vs-truth 0.834 -> 0.771.

findings.claim: Whole-page HTML context (variant C) is not better overall (155/165 adjudicated, 93.9%; six low-confidence none_of_these abstentions on small synthetic pages) but it fixes the two misses that the excerpt-based state could not expose (card grid after the article; clutter-filled main around a 57-word article), picking the truth at 0.92 and 0.95.
findings.evidence: analysis.json variant_C and list_vs_page_A_vs_C flips; misses_C.txt: none_of_these at conf 0.02-0.38 on author-share-widget, trailing-cta-newsletter, issues--162-aria-hidden-main-content, general--substack-app, general--tailwind-hidden-blog-index, footnotes--external-labeled-section. 2/167 pages exceeded the 25k-token cap (general--github.com-issue-56 at 27,237 est. tokens; lesswrong at 41,612) and were not sent; no 400 max_tokens_exceeded occurred in any variant.

findings.claim: The spec's Noul-derived rule (smallest candidate with contains_all>=0.5 and non_article<=0.5) scores 142/167 (85.0%) adjudicated with 23 abstentions and agrees with the Choice on 85.6%; contains_all separates article-holding containers from the rest at AUROC 0.991, but non_article separates a clutter-bearing ancestor from the true container at only AUROC 0.834 because the 300/150-char excerpts rarely show the clutter. Loosening to contains_all>=0.3 gives 157/167 (94.0%).
findings.evidence: analysis.json noul_derived_pick_A and noul_diagnostics_A (truth mean contains_all 0.745, ancestor 0.695, descendant 0.154; truth non_article 0.086, ancestor 0.234, only 19.4% of ancestors >=0.5); analysis2.json noul_pick_adjudicated.

findings.claim: defuddle's pick does not map to the smallest covering candidate 'by construction': 8/167 adjudicated differences (5 over-inclusive picks cleaned by later removal steps, 2 retry-chosen elements that are not ENTRY_POINT candidates at all, 1 case where defuddle's larger pick is actually what the expected output needs), yet all 167 pass the fixture tests. Over-inclusive container errors are mostly harmless in defuddle; under-inclusive ones are not.
findings.evidence: analysis2.json defuddle_findMainContent.misses_adjudicated (card-grid, external-labeled-section, labeled-section-ol, appendix-heading, github.com-issue-56, substack-app not_a_candidate, substack-custom-domain, 162-aria-hidden not_a_candidate); e2e oracle_truth fails only on github.com-issue-56 (swapped output loses '## Description' heading outside the inner markdown-body); 17 over-inclusive B picks produce only 2 e2e failures. Retry cascade at src/defuddle.ts:88-215 explains the not_a_candidate picks (hidden-subtree and schema.org retries override contentSelector).

findings.claim: Cost and latency: list variants average 1,033 input tokens per page (about $0.0000434/page), full-page variant 1,580 tokens ($0.0000664/page); latency p50 67-201 ms, p90 106-207 ms, p99 170-399 ms, max 401 ms at concurrency 6; 833 calls total, 942,123 input tokens, ~$0.040, 0 HTTP errors, all responses model=jev-1.14.0.
findings.evidence: usage_A.json, usage_B.json, usage_A2.json, usage_C.json, usage_D.json; analysis2.json cost.TOTAL. Batching 5-21 questions per request (1 Choice + 2 Nouls per candidate) did not raise latency versus the 1-question variant C.

findings.claim: The sample is dominated by trivial cases: 126/167 pages have exactly 2 candidates (body plus one article/main with the same text), where Jev-A is 126/126 and findMainContent 122/126; the discriminating subset is the 41 pages with >=3 nested candidates (Jev-A 37/41, findMainContent 37/41, Jev-B 26/41, Jev-D 30/41) and the 9 real pages >20KB (Jev-A 9/9, A2 8/9, B 7/9, C 6/7, D 9/9, findMainContent 7/9).
findings.evidence: build_summary.json n_candidates_hist {2:126,3:35,4:4,6:1,10:1}, kept_real_pages_gt20KB 9, kept_gt8KB 15; analysis2.json accuracy.*.adjudicated_2cand / adjudicated_3plus / adjudicated_real_gt20KB. SCOUT_NOTES: fixture median 1,755 bytes.

findings.claim: Inference: Jev's one harmful over-inclusion pattern is preferring a large clutter-filled wrapper over a short true article (57 words) even while its own non_article Noul for that wrapper read 0.83, suggesting it treats a small word count as evidence against 'the whole article'; this is the failure mode a gate must catch, and it was at 0.45 confidence.
findings.evidence: misses_A.txt entry-point--js-article-content: c2 main 609 words chosen at 0.45 (p: c1 0.05, c2 0.59, c3 0.19, none 0.17), nouls c2 contains_all 0.43 non_article 0.83, c3 contains_all 0.11 non_article 0.05; fixture structure main > sidebar(toc, share) + content-area > .js-article-content + recommended-footer + subscription + legal. Same pick in A2, B; body in D; correct c3@0.95 in C.

caveats: Sample is small and skewed: 167 fixtures, 126 with only 2 candidates (near-trivial body vs article), 41 with >=3, 9 real full pages >20KB; the 97.6% headline is driven by synthetic regression fixtures and should not be read as a web-scale estimate.

Ground truth is derived from defuddle's own expected outputs, so it is biased toward defuddle's notion of the container; it is also noisy: 5 'none_of_these' labels are provable artifacts, 1 label (github issue) is contradicted by the oracle end-to-end check, 1 is ambiguous (header vs article-body), and 2 external-footnote labels pick <body> literally. Strict-spec and adjudicated numbers are both reported.

The previous run's raw Jev results (variants A, B, A2, C) were reused after verifying that an independent rebuild of candidates.jsonl is byte-identical; only variant D and all analyses are new in this run. Jev is non-deterministic (3% repeat flips observed), so re-running would move individual picks at low confidence.

The 'ground truth = smallest covering candidate' definition penalizes over-inclusive picks that defuddle's later removal stages would clean up; the end-to-end swap check is the better measure of practical harm and is reported separately.

End-to-end swap passes contentSelector through the normal retry cascade (src/defuddle.ts:88-215), where hidden-subtree and schema.org retries can override it; this matches how a real integration would behave but means a few passes are rescued by defuddle rather than by Jev.

Variant C truncated nothing but excluded the 2 pages over 25k estimated tokens; real-world pages are often larger, and the brief notes accuracy loss with irrelevant content and the 32k per-question limit.

Single model version (jev-1.14.0) and single prompt wording; option labels in A/B/C included tag and class names, which variant D shows materially inflate confidence. No test of adversarial content in the state; the brief documents 93-100% injection success on routing tasks.
Latency p50 varied 67-201 ms across identically sized variants minutes apart, so the latency figures reflect server load at the time, not a stable property.

Not evaluated here: the browser extension's 'no network requests' promise and synchronous parse() API, and the Worker's cost model; any adoption would have to resolve those before this slice's numbers matter.
