result.verdict_for_this_dimension: Measured: on 167 fixtures (126 trivial two-candidate pages, 41 with nested wrappers, 9 real pages) jev-1.14.0 names the smallest covering container 97.6% of the time (adjudicated; 94.0% on strict labels) versus 95.2% for defuddle's findMainContent, and a confidence>=0.5 Jev pick with findMainContent as fallback reproduces 167/167 expected outputs; ungated it breaks 3 fixtures (2 harmfully), reversing option order flips 9.6% of picks (63% accuracy on 3+-candidate pages), and removing tag/class names from the state drops it to 88.0% with no confident picks, showing most of its signal restates the ENTRY_POINT_ELEMENTS heuristic. Verdict: Jev is roughly a peer of findMainContent, not a step toward 99.99%; the only defensible role is a confidence-gated shadow or tie-break signal on pages with three or more nested candidates (ideally with full-page context), never the sole selector, and its end-to-end parity here is borrowed from defuddle's own fallback and downstream clutter removal.

result.title: Runtime, product and operational constraints on inserting a hosted decision-model (Jev) call into Defuddle, per environment
result.summary:
I read the entry points, option plumbing, Worker, privacy/terms/pricing pages, CI and test harness in /home/alexi/git/defuddle (0.19.6 @ 3e8bde9), built the browser bundles to measure them against the CI budgets, ran the perf suite under both DOM backends, and verified four external facts with live fetches (Obsidian Web Clipper source and package.json, Cloudflare Workers limits page, Workers AI typesafe/jev model page, Workers AI pricing/limits pages). Nothing in the repo was modified; outputs are under /tmp/jev-research/results/runtime-constraints/.

Measured facts that bound the design: (1) The removal pipeline (`parseInternal`, src/defuddle.ts:811) is synchronous and is called up to six times by the word-count retry cascade (`_parseWithRetries`, :88-215); `parse()` (:73) is a public sync API used by the full bundle (src/index.full.ts:20-24), by the Worker playground route (website/src/convert.ts:22-27 via index.ts:368-380), by conversation extractors (src/extractors/_conversation.ts:26) and by the Obsidian clipper's `parseForClip` (clip-utils.ts, verified). An `await` inside the pipeline is therefore impossible without a breaking change; a model call can only be a pre-pass or post-pass around `parseInternal`, triggered from `parseAsync()` (:737-760), `defuddle/node` (src/node.ts:41), the CLI (src/cli.ts:84) and the Worker URL route (convert.ts:18-20, 129-202), all of which are already async. (2) Current parse time: linkedom p50 16 ms / p90 53 / p99 207 / max 418 ms over 226 fixtures; JSDOM p50 65 / p90 184 / p99 659 / max 1306 ms. A single Jev round trip (100-800 ms per the brief; Cloudflare-measured 524 ms median) is 6-30x the median parse. (3) Bundle budgets: core 90.2 KB gzip against a 92 KB budget (1.8 KB headroom), full 207.3/215 KB. A minimal hand-written client minifies to 705 B gzip and fits; the official `@typesafe-ai/sdk` 0.7.0 is 338,733 bytes unpacked and declares `engines.node >=22` while CI's floor is Node 20 (ci.yml:23), so the SDK is out for both bundles and CI. (4) The privacy page sentence "The npm package and browser extension run entirely locally and make no network requests." (website/src/privacy.ts:31, added 2026-03-14 in e58ecf4) was already inaccurate when written: `parseAsync`/`extractAsync` landed 2026-03-03 (f85fe52), five extractors declare `prefersAsync()` and fetch network-first (YouTube InnerTube, Reddit, bilibili, c2 wiki, X oEmbed/FxTwitter), `useAsync` defaults to true, and the clipper 1.7.1 calls `await parseAsync()` (raced against an ~8 s timeout, falling back to `parse()`) with no `useAsync:false`. README's "Third-party services" section (README.md:298-302) lists only FxTwitter. Any default-on model call would turn an incomplete disclosure into a plainly false one and would ship page text, including logged-in content (a Gmail extractor exists), to a US-hosted third party that had an output-leak incident on Oct 24.

For the Worker: Workers AI exposes `typesafe/jev` at $0.042/M input, $0 output, "Zero data retention: Yes", 32,000-token context, but its sample responses return jev-1.13.0 (not 1.14), billing is "still in neurons in the back end" with 10,000 free neurons/day and the Workers Paid plan required beyond that, and no rate-limit row exists for this model. wrangler.toml (lines 1-28) has no `[ai]` binding and the `Env` type (website/src/index.ts:26-32) has no `AI` member, so this is a config + type change rather than a new secret. Workers limits verified today: CPU 10 ms free / 30 s default, 5 min max paid (network wait is not CPU), HTTP wall-clock "No limit", 50/10,000 subrequests, 6 concurrent connections, 128 MB; whether `env.AI.run` counts as a subrequest is not stated. The Worker has no overall deadline; `FETCH_TIMEOUT` is 10 s per page fetch (src/fetch.ts:3) with a possible second 10 s bot-UA retry, 5 MB max page, 4 s for YouTube oEmbed; results are edge-cached with `s-maxage=300` (index.ts:17, 637). Revenue is $0.005/$0.004/$0.003 per paid request (pricing.ts:10,20,30; index.ts:20-24) and $0 for the 1,000/month/IP free tier (terms.ts:28). A model call costs 0.8% of revenue at 1k input tokens, 4-7% at 5k, 27-45% at the 32k per-question maximum; the task's $0.0004-0.004 range is 8%-133% of revenue. Because the state is billed once per request and questions are nearly free, one batched request per page is the cost shape; fixture decision points per page are p50 3, p90 11, p99 54, max 213.

Testing: tests/fixtures.test.ts:104-105 injects a rejecting `fetch` and compares output byte-for-byte after attribute normalization (:120); CI (ci.yml) runs that under Node 20/22/24 x linkedom/JSDOM with no secrets. With the brief's 12% chosen-option flip rate, the probability that a page's output is identical on rerun is 0.88^N: 53% at 5 decisions, 28% at 10, 0.17% at 50, so an un-cached live model cannot be under byte-equal tests at all. The feasible scheme is record/replay keyed on (pinned model, sha256 of whitespace-normalized state, sha256 of questions) with recordings committed as JSON; one full-suite recording pass over all 226 fixtures' visible text is ~99,760 tokens (~$0.004), but recordings go stale on any wording change and can only be refreshed by a key holder (not by fork PRs). Verdict for this dimension: a hosted decision model is insertable only as an opt-in, async-only, fail-open, cached pre/post-pass in Node, CLI and the Worker (Workers AI binding being the lowest-friction Worker path); it is effectively blocked in the browser/clipper environments by key custody, the privacy promise, the sync `parse()` contract in the clipper's clip path, content-script fetch restrictions and the 1.8 KB bundle headroom; and "aggressive" (default-on, hot-path, all-environments) use is ruled out by these runtime constraints alone. The deterministic security sanitizer (`_stripUnsafeElements`, src/defuddle.ts:1084-1090, unconditional) must remain the only guaranteed boundary; no network-dependent step can be ~99.99% reliable when the transport (429/529, "no guarantees" terms, 12% flip) is not.

findings.claim: The removal pipeline is synchronous and multiply-invoked; a model call cannot be awaited inside it without breaking the public sync parse() contract, so any Jev integration must be a pre-pass or post-pass around parseInternal, driven only from already-async entry points.
findings.evidence: parse() is sync at src/defuddle.ts:73 and calls _parse()/_parseWithRetries (:78-88); _parseWithRetries calls parseInternal() up to six times with different overrideOptions (:99, :104, :123, :141, :165, :198); parseInternal is declared sync at :811 and is also called recursively for extractor contentSelector runs (:873). parseAsync (:737-760) itself calls the sync this._parse() at :746 and only awaits tryAsyncExtractor (:787-807). Sync parse() consumers: src/index.full.ts:20-24, website/src/convert.ts:15 and :22-27 (POST /api/parse at website/src/index.ts:368-380), src/extractors/_conversation.ts:26, and the Obsidian clipper's clip-utils.ts parseForClip (verified by fetch: `new Defuddle(doc, { url: doc.URL }).parse()` from 'defuddle/full'). Async-capable call sites today: Defuddle.parseAsync (src/defuddle.ts:737), fetchAsyncVariables (:767), src/node.ts:41 (`await defuddle.parseAsync()`), src/cli.ts:84 (`await Defuddle(doc, url, defuddleOpts)`), website/src/convert.ts:18-20 defuddleHtmlAsync used by convertToHtml (:129-154) and convertToMarkdown (:156-202), and the clipper's content.ts (`await Promise.race([defuddle.parseAsync(), parseTimeout]).catch(() => defuddle.parse())`).

findings.claim: The existing options.fetch plumbing is the only network seam and already reaches every extractor; a decisionModel option could reuse it, but tests inject a rejecting fetch, so in CI the model path would always fail and must fail open to the deterministic result.
findings.evidence: DefuddleOptions.fetch at src/types.ts:151-156 ("Useful in environments where the global fetch has restrictions (e.g. browser extensions that need to proxy requests)"); threaded into ExtractorOptions at src/defuddle.ts:773, :793, :861-865 and src/extractors/_base.ts:3-7; BaseExtractor.fetch getter falls back to globalThis.fetch at _base.ts:22-24. tests/fixtures.test.ts:104-105 passes `fetch: () => Promise.reject(new Error('network disabled in fixture tests'))`; tests/perf.test.ts:14-17 and tests/twitter-linkedom.test.ts do the same; tests/preferred-async.test.ts and tests/degraded-fallback.test.ts call parseAsync without a fetch override (they rely on extractor-level behavior).

findings.claim: The privacy page's claim that the npm package and browser extension make no network requests is already inaccurate today, and README's third-party disclosure is incomplete; a default-on model call would make both plainly false.
findings.evidence: website/src/privacy.ts:31: "The npm package and browser extension run entirely locally and make no network requests." (page 'updated March 14, 2026', privacy.ts:41; sentence introduced in commit e58ecf4 2026-03-14 'Meter API (#173)'). parseAsync/extractAsync were introduced in f85fe52 2026-03-03 and useAsync (default true) in f8ce8a4 2026-03-03 (src/types.ts:88-92). Five extractors override prefersAsync() (src/extractors/youtube.ts:87, reddit.ts:96, bilibili.ts:81, c2-wiki.ts:18, x-oembed.ts:132) and ExtractorRegistry.findPreferredAsyncExtractor (src/extractor-registry.ts:251-252) runs them FIRST in parseAsync (src/defuddle.ts:738-742) regardless of local content, contradicting README.md:300 ("This only happens when the page HTML contains no usable content"). Hosts fetched: api.fxtwitter.com, publish.twitter.com/oembed, www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player and /next, reddit.com (old.reddit/Atom), api.bilibili.com, c2.com/wiki/remodel/pages. README.md:298-302 lists only FxTwitter. The Obsidian clipper 1.7.1 (package.json `"defuddle": "^0.19.2"`) calls `await Promise.race([defuddle.parseAsync(), parseTimeout])` in content.ts with options `{ url: document.URL }` only, so useAsync stays true in the extension.

findings.claim: In the browser/clipper environment there is no safe place for a hosted-model API key and no caller-side plumbing to supply one; the only options are BYOK stored by the extension or a proxy someone else pays for.
findings.evidence: Core bundle is a UMD 'web' target with zero runtime deps (webpack.config.js:48-74; package.json:78-81); any key compiled in is public (brief: "No browser-safe mode: a key shipped in client code is exposed"). Clipper content.ts constructs `new Defuddle(document, { url: document.URL })` with no fetch/useAsync/apiKey option and returns results via sendResponse (message passing), so defuddle has no channel to a key without a clipper change. Clipper README fetched today describes no BYOK/LLM feature and package.json has no LLM SDK dependency. The content script runs with the page's privileges, and a Gmail extractor exists (tests/extractor-attributes.test.ts:44 uses GMAIL_URL), so page state sent to the model may include logged-in private content. Brief: TypeSafe is US-hosted, ZDR only via enterprise sales, Oct 24 incident exposed customers' noul outputs.

findings.claim: Bundle budgets leave 1.8 KB (core) and 7.7 KB (full) gzip headroom; a minimal ~50-line HTTP client (705 B gzip) fits, the official JS SDK does not fit anywhere and cannot run on CI's Node 20 floor.
findings.evidence: Built with `npm run build:js`; scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs output: dist/index.js 90.2 KB gzip / 92 KB budget, dist/index.full.js 207.3 KB gzip / 215 KB budget (raw 340,738 and 770,629 bytes). Budgets at scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs:7-10 ("~10% headroom ... bump them deliberately"); enforced in CI build job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:44-56). Earlier-attempt artifact /tmp/jev-research/results/runtime-constraints/jev-client-sample.min.js: 1,112 bytes minified, 705 bytes gzip. `npm view @typesafe-ai/sdk`: version 0.7.0, dist.unpackedSize 338,733, fileCount 9, engines.node '>=22'; CI matrix is node [20, 22, 24] (ci.yml:23) and the comment at ci.yml:15-16 fixes the floor at 20.

findings.claim: Current parse time is small relative to one model round trip: a single Jev call would add 6-30x the median parse time, and the clipper already imposes an ~8 s total race on parseAsync.
findings.evidence: Measured with tests/perf.test.ts (network disabled, profile:true) on this machine, 226 fixtures: linkedom parse min 3 / p50 16 / p75 27 / p90 53 / p95 81 / p99 207 / max 418 ms (sum 6,731 ms; DOM parse 196 ms = 3%); JSDOM parse min 12 / p50 65 / p75 105 / p90 184 / p95 257 / p99 659 / max 1,306 ms (sum 23,425 ms). Slowest: substack-app 418 ms, lesswrong 348 ms, mathjax 280 ms (linkedom). Per-step share (linkedom): removeBySelector 23%, standardizeContent 20%, standardizeElements 10%, findMainContent 10%, removeByContentPattern 8%, removeLowScoring 4%. Brief/excerpts: Jev p50 100-500 ms direct, 500-800 ms via gateways, Cloudflare-measured 524 ms median. Clipper content.ts races parseAsync against a timeout (reported ~8 s by the fetched source summary) then falls back to sync parse(). Raw outputs: /tmp/jev-research/results/runtime-constraints/perf-linkedom.txt and perf-jsdom.txt.

findings.claim: For the Worker, Workers AI's typesafe/jev is usable without an outbound key and with ZDR, but it requires adding an [ai] binding and the Paid plan, returns jev-1.13.0 rather than 1.14, and has no published rate limit for this model.
findings.evidence: Fetched https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai/models/typesafe/jev/ today: model id `typesafe/jev` via `env.AI.run`; pricing $0.042 per 1M input tokens, $0.00 output, $0.00 cached input; "Zero data retention | Yes"; provider "Third-party"; context "32,000 tokens"; sample responses return "jev-1.13.0"; question types shown noul/choice/score (no box); REST alternative uses CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN. Workers AI pricing page: "10,000 Neurons per day at no charge", $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons above that, "still billing in neurons in the back end", "To use more than 10,000 Neurons per day, you need to sign up for the Workers Paid plan"; no typesafe/jev row. Workers AI limits page: no row for typesafe/jev or decision models; generic text-generation default 300 rpm (applicability unknown); whether env.AI.run counts toward subrequest limits: not stated. Repo: website/wrangler.toml:1-28 declares only KV RATE_LIMIT and two Durable Objects, no [ai]; Env type at website/src/index.ts:26-32 has no AI member; website/worker-configuration.d.ts:8671-8724 already declares `abstract class Ai` with `run<Name>(model, inputs, options)`, so the types are present.

findings.claim: Workers platform limits do not block a model call: HTTP wall-clock is unlimited, CPU is 30 s default (5 min max) on Paid and network wait is not CPU, but the Free plan's 10 ms CPU would already be exceeded by current parse times, implying the Worker is on Paid.
findings.evidence: Fetched https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ today: CPU time per HTTP request 10 ms (Free) / 5 min, default 30 s via limits.cpu_ms (Paid); Duration 'HTTP request: No limit'; waitUntil up to 30 s after response; subrequests 50 (Free) / 10,000 up to 10M (Paid); six simultaneous connections per invocation; 128 MB memory; Cache API max object 512 MB. Measured linkedom parse p50 16 ms, p99 207 ms exceeds 10 ms CPU, and the Worker uses Durable Objects (wrangler.toml:20-28). Inference: production runs on Workers Paid (not directly verifiable from the repo).

findings.claim: The Worker's request timing budget is dominated by page fetches (10 s per fetch, possibly twice), with a 5-minute edge cache; it sets no overall deadline, so a 0.5 s model call fits but adds to the already-uncapped tail.

Token counts use chars/4 on visible text as an estimate; Jev's tokenizer was not used. Obsidian Web Clipper facts (defuddle ^0.19.2, parseAsync raced against a timeout, {url} only, clip-utils sync parse) come from WebFetch summaries of main-branch source today; the timeout value (~8 s) is as reported by that summary and was not read verbatim. My recollection that the clipper ships an 'Interpreter' BYOK feature is NOT confirmed by the README fetched today and should be treated as unverified.

Whether production defuddle.md runs on Workers Paid is inferred from parse times exceeding the Free plan's 10 ms CPU limit and from Durable Object use; not directly verifiable from the repo. Whether env.AI.run counts toward subrequest limits and what rate limit applies to typesafe/jev on Workers AI are 'not stated' on the pages fetched.

Workers AI pricing is in neurons; the $0.042/M figure on the model page is the token-equivalent and the pricing page says billing is 'still in neurons in the back end'. The model page's sample responses show jev-1.13.0; whether 1.14 is served was not verifiable.

Cost-fraction math assumes state billed once per request (brief's 447-token/3-question example) and ignores cache hits (s-maxage=300) which would reduce effective per-request model cost by the cache hit rate, which is unknown.

No live Jev API calls were made in this slice; nothing here measures model accuracy. `npm view` and WebFetch were used for public metadata only; no key was read or printed. The repo stayed clean apart from untracked dist/ build output (npm run build:js was run to measure bundle sizes).
result.verdict_for_this_dimension: Runtime and product constraints permit a hosted decision model only as an opt-in, async-only, fail-open, cached pre/post-pass around the synchronous pipeline, and only in Node, CLI and the Worker; the Worker via the Workers AI `typesafe/jev` binding (no key, ZDR, $0.042/M, 4-7% of per-request revenue at typical state sizes, but Paid plan, `[ai]` binding, privacy-page edits and jev-1.13.0) is the lowest-friction place to run a shadow-mode trial. The browser/Obsidian clipper environment is effectively blocked (no safe key custody, the "make no network requests" privacy promise, content-script fetch restrictions, 1.8 KB gzip headroom, the clip path's sync parse(), and user-visible non-determinism). The byte-equal, secret-free, dual-DOM CI can only cover the model path through committed record/replay keyed on a pinned model and normalized state. "Aggressive" use (default-on, in the hot path, across environments) is ruled out by these constraints alone, and "~99.99% reliable" cannot be achieved by any network-dependent step; the unconditional deterministic sanitizer must remain the sole guaranteed boundary.

result.title: Defuddle meaning-B (clutter removal / main-content extraction): decision-point inventory, uncertainty gates, failure-class history, and where a Jev Noul/Choice could plug in
result.summary:
I read the full extraction pipeline (src/defuddle.ts _parseWithRetries L88-215, parseInternal L811-1130, findMainContent L1242-1319, findTableBasedContent L1321-1358, findContentByScoring L1360-1370; src/removals/{scoring,selectors,content-patterns,hidden,metadata-block,small-images}.ts; src/content-boundary.ts; src/constants.ts) and produced an inventory of 51 decision points. Only 4 of them are fuzzy text-readable judgments in the pure sense (the 35-word navigationIndicators scorer, the 11 BOILERPLATE_PATTERNS, the newsletter/related/CTA heading regexes, the screen-reader-annotation regex); 13 are deterministic attribute/tag rules (EXACT_SELECTORS 162 entries, PARTIAL_SELECTORS 547 regex fragments over class/id/data-test* attributes, hidden-style/Tailwind tokens, pre/code/footnote/data-defuddle protections); the remaining ~34 are numeric thresholds (I counted ~28 numeric comparisons in scoring.ts, ~85 in content-patterns.ts, 6 in the retry cascade) wrapped around structural/positional facts (is this above the first prose paragraph, does prose follow, is it the last child, is the h1 adjacent, is the child inside the top candidate, is the cell bigger than half the body). The signature of this codebase is that almost every "fuzzy" rule is a text regex AND a position check AND a word-count band, so the evidence is only half "literally present" in a block.

Measured on the 226 fixtures (instrumented dist build, offline; I verified the earlier attempt's measure-gates.mjs and independently reproduced its per-step removal totals 1778/52/50/48/10): removeBySelector does 91.8% of all removals (1,218 exact + 560 partial; 75 distinct partial patterns fired, 'footer' 90x, 'menu-' 48x, 'avatar' 36x); scoreAndRemove removes 52 blocks of 502 scored (408 score exactly 0, 41 nonzero within +/-5, 62 within +/-10); isLikelyContent protects 658 of 1,160 blocks it sees; content patterns remove 50 across 34 rule families (none fires more than 5 times); findMainContent picks the top-scored candidate in 205/211 fixtures, has top-2 margin <80 in 14 (6.6%), and lands on <body> in 25 (11.8%); the <200-word retry fires on 163/226 first passes and the <50 gate on 54, but retries change the final result in only 11 fixtures (fixtures are tiny, median 1.7 KB, so these rates overstate the web). The explicit uncertainty gates number 5 (word-count <200, <50 hidden, hidden-selector, <50 index-page, schema 1.5x) plus 6 implicit ones (candidate margin, child-preference tie, body fallback, score near 0, isLikelyContent borderline, findContentStart returning null which silently disables all pre-content rules).

Failure-class history: of 781 commits, the earlier keyword pass gives infra/docs/deps 293, formatting 186, clutter-removal rules 161, site extractors 80, metadata 25, security 20, main-content selection 14; my sub-classification of 277 extraction-related subjects finds 115 are plain selector-list additions (attribute-token rules, 71% of clutter commits), 52 content-pattern rules (text+structure), 33 container/retry/fallback, 28 explicit "keep content / overly aggressive" repairs (#107/#77 'appendix'/'enhancement', #112 nav words in prose, 0699bb0 breadcrumb lists, 29872c0 trailing-section conclusion, #284 header cells, #286 duplicate images, #358 whole-body fallback), 9 scoring. Of 244 GitHub issues (61 open) classified by title: infra 50, formatting 46, site-extractor 42, main-container/page-structure 30, clutter-FP attribute-rule 21, clutter-FP structural-rule 15, clutter-FP text-heuristic 12, images 8, clutter-FN structural 7, metadata 6, clutter-FN kept-clutter 6. Among the 99 extraction-proper issues, 39 (39%) are text-readable (the block's own content shows it is prose; 21 of these were killed by an attribute token) and 60 (61%) are structural; among open extraction issues it is 11 text-readable vs 20 structural. Formatting (math/code/footnotes/markdown) is 19% of issues, 37% of fixture families and co-changes with 50% of the 196 expected-output commits, and no keep/remove classifier touches it. A live 18-block probe (jev-1.14.0, 5 Nouls per block, $0.00044, p50 65 ms) got 16/18 with a code-owned policy: all 3 attribute-rule FPs (#444, #441, #371) and 9/10 text cases were judged correctly from the block alone; the #445 "Comment" truncation case was wrong alone (P(body)=0.44) and right only when code supplied the next sibling (0.52 vs 0.16 for a real comments section), confirming the text/structural split. The sibling block experiment on 1,475 fixture blocks measured 83.7% accuracy, AUROC 0.838, 66.9% on 3-5-word blocks, and only 40% agreement on container-level removals.

Implication for the Jev question: a per-block "keep?" Noul can plausibly address the text-readable 39% of extraction failures if plugged in as a confidence-gated veto at three specific sites (partial-selector removals of prose-bearing elements, scorer blocks in the [-20,+10] band, and the boilerplate/related-heading trailing-cascade truncations), with code supplying position facts in the state. It cannot address the structural 61% (wrong container, hidden/aria-hidden content, listing pages, retries, images) except via a "which container?" Choice over code-built candidates, and it cannot touch formatting. "99.99%" has no meaning for extraction except page-level identical-to-expected; at 50-200 block decisions per real page, that would require ~1e-6 per-block error, five orders of magnitude beyond the measured 0.84 block accuracy or the 0.95 high-confidence band, and Jev's 12% repeat-flip rate is incompatible with byte-equal fixture tests without caching. Verdict: narrow, gated, opt-in, shadow-mode first; not aggressive, and not a path to four nines.

The 6 non-top picks are the child-preference rule (defuddle.ts L1297-1316) or table fallback (L1321-1358): entry-point--js-article-content, maggieappleton (margin 39.8 main vs article), gated-content--cookie-consent, general--substack-app, table-layout--blogger-two-column, table-layout--paulgraham.

findings.claim: The retry cascade's explicit uncertainty gates fire constantly on fixtures but almost never change the answer: <200-word gate on 163/226 first passes, <50 on 54, yet the final result differs from the first pass in only 11 fixtures (544 parseInternal calls total).
findings.evidence: gates-summary.json retry_kinds: initial 231, removePartialSelectors 182, removeHiddenElements 64, index-page 57, hidden-contentSelector 7, schema contentSelector 1. Fixtures are small (median 1,755 bytes) so the word-count gates overfire relative to real pages. Retry-changed examples: author-contact-block 0->236 words (partial selectors had removed everything), issues--162-aria-hidden 2->86, issues--361-* 5->170.

findings.claim: Historically, 71% of clutter-removal commits (115/161) are bare additions to the selector lists, and the lists grew from 333 partial / 91 exact (v0.3.0) to 547 / 162 (HEAD); 28 commits are explicit 'keep content / overly aggressive' repairs.
findings.evidence: classify-failures.mjs over gitlog_all.txt; selector counts from git show <tag>:src/constants.ts at 0.3.0, 0.3.7, 0.5.3, 0.6.4, 0.10.0, 0.15.0, 0.19.1, HEAD. Repairs include 9e6fa75 (#112 word-boundary + prose protection), ae6fc5c (#107/#77: 'appendix' commented out, 'enhancement' -> 'enhancement-'), 29872c0 (nango: require <2 prose paragraphs before trailing-section removal; strip heading ids from partial matching), 0699bb0 (breadcrumb list items <=8 words), 0e206c0 (#358 whole-body fallback).

findings.claim: Of 244 GitHub issues, 99 are extraction-proper; 39 (39%) are text-readable from the block's own content (12 text-heuristic FPs such as #112 nav words, #428 'register', #445 'Comment', #284 header cells, plus 21 attribute-rule FPs such as #444 id=term-related-claim, #441 [data-date], #321 id=tags, #279 hero, #252 [href*=/author/], #131, #132, #106, and 6 kept-clutter FNs) and 60 (61%) are structural (wrong container, aria-hidden, listing pages, lazy images, trailing-cascade truncation). Open extraction issues: 11 text-readable vs 20 structural.
findings.evidence: Hand classification by issue title in classify-failures.mjs -> failure-classes.json (issueByClass / openByClass). Overall: infra 50, formatting 46, site-extractor 42, main-container 30, clutter-FP-attr 21, clutter-FP-struct 15, clutter-FP-text 12, images 8, clutter-FN-struct 7, metadata 6, clutter-FN-text 6, unclassified 1 (#66).

findings.claim: Formatting (math/code/footnotes/markdown/headings/whitespace) is the largest single class of work and is untouched by any keep/remove classifier: 186/781 commits, 46/244 issues, 83/226 fixture families (footnotes 28, elements 19, codeblocks 16, math 14, headings 3, others), and 98 of the 196 commits that changed tests/expected touched src/elements|markdown|standardize (66 touched only those).
findings.evidence: git log --name-only per commit touching tests/expected (expected-commit-areas.txt): formatting 98, constants 51, removals 45, core 44, extractors 21; removals/constants-without-formatting 48; formatting-only 66. Fixture prefix counts via ls tests/fixtures.

findings.claim: A per-block Noul set reads the attribute-rule and text-heuristic failure classes correctly from the block alone but needs code-supplied neighbour context for the trailing-cascade class: live probe 16/18 (text 9/10, attr 3/3, struct 1/2, struct+context 2/2, policy 1/1).

probe-failure-classes.mjs, jev-1.14.0, 18 calls, 10,398 input tokens, $0.000437, latency p50 65 ms / p90 118 ms. #444 P(body)=0.82, #441 0.97, #371 0.59, #112 0.87, #428 0.78, #284 0.79; cookie banner P(chrome)=0.93, byline P(meta)=0.98, newsletter P(cta)=0.98, ToC P(links)=0.98. Misses: '

Comment

' alone P(body)=0.44 (with next sibling of prose 0.52 keep; with a comments-thread sibling 0.16 remove); a content list of long internal links judged P(link_list)=0.94 (the 0699bb0 ambiguity). Single run, hand-written blocks, untuned thresholds.

findings.claim: At fixture scale the sibling block experiment measured Jev at 83.7% block accuracy (AUROC 0.838) with block-only state, 66.9% on 3-5-word blocks (the zone content-patterns operate in), 86.8% agreement with removeBySelector removals but only 40.1% with container-level ('unmatched') removals; |2p-1|>=0.8 covers 66.4% at 89.8%.
findings.evidence: Read from /tmp/jev-research/results/exp-block-classification/analysis-stdout.txt (n=1,475 units from 224 fixtures; not re-run by me). The h1 row (47 removed by Defuddle's title-dedupe policy, Jev keeps them) shows policy decisions must stay in code.

findings.claim: Per-page call volume is bounded and cheap: fixtures average 6.6 candidate blocks (median 3, max 213 on the 200 KB lesswrong page), median 276 chars of cleaned HTML per block; a 200-block real page is roughly 30k input tokens, ~$0.0013, and can be batched as many Nouls per request.
findings.evidence: /tmp/jev-research/results/dataset/blocks.jsonl per-fixture counts (lesswrong 213 units/122k chars, maggieappleton 101/48k, 12gramsofcarbon 54/52k, x.com article 43/48k). Jev brief: 32k tokens per question, questions batch nearly free.

findings.claim: Protections that must stay deterministic regardless of any model: unconditional _stripUnsafeElements on the final root (defuddle.ts L1087), pre/code and td/th skips in scoring (scoring.ts L268-285), pre/code skips in selectors (selectors.ts L43, L83), footnote container/backref protection (selectors.ts L166-177; scoring.ts L452-456), [data-defuddle] extractor output (scoring.ts L273; selectors.ts L76), math under display:none (hidden.ts L22-25), paywall aria-hidden exception (constants.ts L83-89), ancestors-of-mainContent (scoring.ts L263; selectors.ts L159), retry acceptance arithmetic (2x, 1.5x, 0.7x), image dedupe/cover URL logic (defuddle.ts L345-491), the 33 px small-image rule, and the title/h1 dedupe policy; model output must never become a selector.
findings.evidence: Line-cited from source; AGENTS.md 'Preserve sanitization regardless of pipeline options'; Jev brief section 8 (state is argued input; routing flips 93-100% under injection; browser-use ad click 91%).

findings.claim: '99.99%' is not an attainable or even well-defined target for extraction: the only ground truth is byte-equal Markdown for 226 fixtures; page-level identical-to-expected at 99.99% with 50-200 independent block decisions per page needs ~1e-6 per-block error, versus measured 0.16 (block-only) and 0.05 even in the top-confidence band; and Jev's ~12% chosen-option flip on repeat breaks byte-equal tests unless every decision is cached.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic from measured rates; Jev brief Section 2 (determinism: none; 12% flips) and Section 3 (confidence >=0.99 band 96.3% on Banking77). exp-block-classification: |2p-1|>=0.9 band 94.6% on 520 blocks.

caveats: Issue classification (Table 4) is by title only and hand-assigned; borderline titles (e.g. 'site X missing data') were put in main-container/page-structure without reading the threads; one issue (#66) left unclassified. Treat +/-5 per class as noise.

The commit sub-classification is keyword-based; the 'main-container/retry/fallback' bucket over-includes ~10 YouTube/metadata fallback commits, and 'other-extraction' is mostly formatting removals. The earlier attempt's coarse classifier (293/186/161/80/25/20/14/2) was reused after reading its rules.

Gate statistics (Table 3) come from the 226 fixtures, which are small hand-made regression cases (median 1,755 bytes, p90 8.8 KB); the word-count retry gates fire on 72% of them but would fire far less on real pages, and candidate counts/margins are similarly fixture-biased. I verified the instrumentation script (measure-gates.mjs) and independently reproduced its per-step removal totals (1778/52/50/48/10) but did not re-execute it.

The live probe is 18 hand-written anonymized blocks, one run, untuned thresholds, no option rotation; it demonstrates evidence locality (text vs structural), not accuracy. Mid-range probabilities (0.44-0.59) decided several cases, exactly the band the brief says is unreliable.
Sibling-slice numbers (1,475-block experiment: 0.837 accuracy, AUROC 0.838; main-container build summary 153/167 heuristic agreement) are quoted from their stdout/JSON and were not re-run here.
Numeric-threshold counts per file are rough regex counts of comparison operators, intended as orders of magnitude.
Line numbers refer to the working tree at commit 3e8bde9 (0.19.6); the repo was not modified (git status clean apart from dist/ and node_modules).

Runtime constraints (browser bundle is synchronous, promises no network requests, cannot hold an API key; Worker is linkedom and most constrained) are another slice's topic but bound any plug-in to the Node/CLI/Worker opt-in path; nothing here assumes Jev in the extension.

No labeled block corpus exists beyond the 226 expected outputs; every threshold in Table 2 is a starting point to be tuned in shadow mode, per the brief's finding that F1-optimal Noul thresholds are task-specific (median 0.35).
result.verdict_for_this_dimension: For clutter removal / main-content extraction (meaning B), Jev is a plausible, cheap (~$0.001 per 200-block page, ~65 ms per call) confidence-gated veto for the text-readable minority of failures: roughly 39% of extraction-proper issues (21 attribute-token false positives like #444/#441/#371 plus 12 text-heuristic false positives like #112/#428/#284 and 6 kept-clutter misses), plugged in at three specific sites (partial-selector removals of prose-bearing elements, scorer blocks in the [-20,+10] band, and the boilerplate/related-heading trailing cascades) with code supplying position facts in the state. It is not a replacement for the pipeline: 61% of extraction issues (and 20 of 31 open ones) are structural (wrong container, aria-hidden content, listing pages, lazy images, cascade truncations) where the evidence is not in the block, formatting is the largest class of work and no keep/remove classifier touches it, 91.8% of actual removals are deterministic selector hits that already work, and measured block accuracy is 0.84 (0.67 on 3-5-word blocks) with ~12% repeat non-determinism. '99.99%' is not a meaningful target for extraction: the only ground truth is byte-equal Markdown on 226 fixtures, and page-level four nines over 50-200 block decisions would need ~1e-6 per-block error, five orders of magnitude beyond anything measured. Recommendation for this dimension: narrow, gated, opt-in (Node/CLI/Worker only), shadow-mode first with a labeled block corpus derived from tests/expected; do not use aggressively; the deterministic protections (sanitization, pre/code/footnote/extractor output/tables, retry arithmetic, image logic) must remain code-owned and the model must never emit a selector.

result.title: Security sanitization (meaning A): full control map, a newly confirmed strip-before-resolve bypass, residual gaps, and why a Jev gate would subtract rather than add
result.summary:
I mapped every security-sanitization control in defuddle 0.19.6 (src/utils/dom.ts, src/defuddle.ts, src/constants.ts, src/standardize.ts, src/markdown.ts, extractors, the innerHTML lint, five XSS test files, five GHSA advisories, and the defuddle.md Worker) and then measured it offline with a round-trip differential harness: 433 probe rows in /tmp/jev-research/results/security-map/roundtrip-v2.mjs plus 126 rows from an earlier attempt's probe.mjs/probe2.mjs that I re-scored, each run under both linkedom (htmlparser2 10.1.0) and JSDOM (parse5) input and re-parsed with JSDOM as the consumer-browser oracle. No Jev API calls were made; none were needed to settle this slice.

Measured headline: the deterministic sanitizer has a live, exploitable ordering bug. In `_sanitizeExtractorHtml` (src/defuddle.ts:1824 strips, :1825 resolves) and `_serializeFallbackBody` (:325 strips, :326 resolves), `stripUnsafeElements` runs BEFORE `resolveRelativeUrls`, whose `resolve()` helper strips leading quotes/backslash-quotes (:1447-1450). A page value `href='"javascript:alert(1)'` passes `isDangerousUrl` (starts with `"`), then resolve turns it into `javascript:alert(1)`. Per boundary 18/28 probe rows leaked an executable URL (identical under linkedom and JSDOM), and it reaches the public API end to end through a real site extractor (x-article: output `<a href="javascript:alert(2)">`) and through the schema.org articleBody fallback that fires on any page. The main pipeline (resolve at :1070, strip at :1087) is immune (0/28) and the Markdown layer catches it (0/14), so HTML consumers are the victims; the worst one is defuddle.md's documented `/html/` mode, which serves `result.content` as `text/html` on its own origin with no CSP/sandbox/nosniff (website/src/index.ts:622-636). The bug has shipped since 0.19.0/0.19.1 (June 2026) and is unreported.

Across the remaining 500+ probe rows I found zero script-execution bypasses: 48 mXSS/encoding/raw-text payloads x 3 option sets x 2 parsers, every classic DOMPurify-bypass shape, SMIL, template, foreignObject, MathML href, entity/whitespace/control obfuscation, abrupt comments, CDATA: all clean. The residual gaps are all non-script and all option- or path-dependent: `meta`/`link` survive only when `removeExactSelectors=false` (not covered by stripUnsafeElements); `srcset`/`data-src`/`poster`/`background` are never URL-checked (inert in modern browsers); the iframe `allow` attribute is allowlisted; SVG elements keep every attribute including `style` (standardize.ts:475-481) so `fill:url(https://attacker)` always survives; `resolveTailwindClasses` writes a page-derived `text-[...]` value straight into `style` (standardize.ts:929-953) in DEFAULT mode; Markdown complex tables keep `style`/`bgcolor` (markdown.ts:875). None of these is XSS; they are tracking, CSS overlay, and permission-delegation vectors.

The pattern matters for the Jev question: all five GHSA advisories (Mar 5, Jun 24, Aug 22, Sep 17, Oct 24 2026) and the bug found today are coverage/ordering defects in a deterministic design: a boundary that did not run the sanitizer, an element type not traversed, a sink not escaped, two steps in the wrong order. None was a failure to judge ambiguous content. A probabilistic classifier cannot repair "the sanitizer did not run here" or "ran before the rewrite"; it adds one more path to miss. As a gate, Jev would trade exact string checks for a model whose state is argued input (93-100% injection ASR, TokenBreak respellings bypassed its toxicity filter, 91% planted-ad clicks), that is non-deterministic (12% chosen-option change on repeat, no seeds), that costs 175-500 ms per call against a measured Defuddle p50 of 149 ms, that cannot run in the synchronous browser bundle or offline CLI, that cannot hold an API key in an extension, and that would ship page content (the Gmail/ChatGPT/Claude extractors exist) off-device against the stated "make no network requests" promise. As a fuzz oracle it is dominated by the exact oracle I used (spec-parser round trip + attribute scan), which found a real bypass at zero cost. The only defensible role is Worker-side telemetry that never touches output, and even that adds little the deterministic oracle does not already give.

Verdict for this dimension: do not use Jev for meaning-A sanitization, aggressively or otherwise. The path to "99.99%" is deterministic and concrete: fix the two ordering bugs (strip after resolve, or make strip the last operation in every boundary and have resolve() stop stripping quotes), collapse the five HTML output boundaries into one typed finalizer, replace the element denylist plus five-attribute URL check with an allowlist serializer (DOMPurify-style per-attribute URL policy; `data:` only on img/source/track/image; drop meta/link/base/form/style regardless of options), add the round-trip differential test under linkedom + JSDOM + a real browser to CI with property-based fuzzing, and put a CSP sandbox on defuddle.md `/html/` responses so an origin XSS is impossible even when the sanitizer is wrong.

findings.claim: NEW, CONFIRMED BYPASS: quote-prefixed dangerous URLs survive on two sanitization boundaries because stripUnsafeElements runs before resolveRelativeUrls, and resolve() strips leading quotes.
findings.evidence: src/defuddle.ts:1820-1827 (_sanitizeExtractorHtml: :1824 this._stripUnsafeElements(container); :1825 this.resolveRelativeUrls(container)); src/defuddle.ts:322-327 (_serializeFallbackBody: :325 strip, :326 resolveContentUrls); src/defuddle.ts:1444-1458 resolve() does `.replace(/^\\?["']+/, '')` then `new URL(normalized, baseUrl)`. src/utils/dom.ts:73-80 isDangerousUrl checks startsWith('javascript:') on the raw value, so `"javascript:alert(1)` passes. Measured (roundtrip-v2-results.json, strict scheme-anchored oracle): A1 _sanitizeExtractorHtml 18/28 rows leak (a href javascript: x5 variants, a href data:text/html, iframe src javascript:, iframe src data:text/html, img src javascript:; each under linkedom and JSDOM); A2 _serializeFallbackBody 18/28; A3 schema.org articleBody fallback end-to-end through Defuddle() 18/28; A4 main pipeline control 0/28 (resolve at :1070 precedes strip at :1087). Output literally contains `click`.

findings.claim: The bypass reaches the public API through a real site extractor and through the schema.org fallback that applies to any page; every one of the 25 site extractors is routed through the vulnerable _sanitizeExtractorHtml.

src/defuddle.ts:1775 buildExtractorResponse -> _sanitizeExtractorHtml; :204 schema fallback -> _sanitizeExtractorHtml(schemaText); :311 _fallbackResponse -> _serializeFallbackBody. Measured A6: x.com article page with header `` and body `` yields content `

findings.claim: Victim with the highest impact: defuddle.md `/html/` mode serves extracted HTML as text/html on the defuddle.md origin with no Content-Security-Policy, sandbox, X-Frame-Options or nosniff, and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *; a crafted page therefore yields origin XSS for anyone opening defuddle.md/html/<url> in a browser (cached 5 min for unauthenticated requests).

Documented feature: website/src/docs-content.ts:124-126. convertToHtml (website/src/convert.ts:129-154) returns result.content unchanged. Origin exposure is limited (API keys travel in Authorization header or ?key= query, :563-569; success page shows a one-time key, website/src/success.ts:101-107); still a stored/reflected XSS on a paid API domain.

findings.claim: The Markdown layer independently neutralizes the bypass, so Markdown consumers (the default for the Obsidian clipper flow and the defuddle.md default endpoint) are not exposed by it.
findings.evidence: Measured A5: schema fallback + {markdown:true} 0/14 strict hits; C createMarkdownContent direct 0/14 (it never resolves URLs so the quote prefix stays and the value is an inert relative URL). Mechanism: src/markdown.ts:70 formatMarkdownLinkDestination returns '' when isDangerousUrl(href); :211-213 sanitizedOuterHTML re-runs stripUnsafeElements on kept elements (iframe/video/audio/sup/sub/svg/math, :365); :893 complex tables re-run it; :240-245 autolink escaping. Whether the Obsidian Web Clipper consumes `content` HTML or Markdown from defuddle is not verifiable from this repo (inference).

findings.claim: Complete control map: the deterministic design is a denylist of 16 element types + on*/srcdoc attribute strip + a 3-scheme URL check on exactly five attributes (href, src, action, formaction, xlink:href), applied at five HTML output boundaries plus two Markdown sub-boundaries, with an optional attribute allowlist and an innerHTML lint.

findings.claim: No parser-differential or mXSS bypass was found between linkedom/htmlparser2 and parse5/JSDOM across the classic vectors.
findings.evidence: Group B: 48 payloads x {default, standardize:false, all-removals-off} x {linkedom, JSDOM} = 288 rows; 0 script-execution hits. Includes DOMPurify-2.0.17 form/math/mglyph/style, mtext/table/mglyph/style, svg>p>style, svg CDATA breakout, annotation-xml text/html, attribute-value tag breakout, hex/tab/control/colon entity javascript:, U+2028, mixed case, iframe javascript:/data: b64, details ontoggle, marquee onstart, svg image/feImage/use/script/handler, object/embed/base, nested anchors, comment smuggling. Prior probe.mjs (51 payload/option combos, both parsers): raw-text-vs-foreign-content differentials (svg>noembed/xmp/noframes/iframe/textarea/title/plaintext, math>mtext>textarea), svg style escape mXSS, abrupt comment, bogus PI, template-in-svg, srcdoc entity, slash-separated img onerror: all clean.

findings.claim: Residual non-script gaps (measured): meta/link survive when removeExactSelectors=false; srcset/data-src/poster/background are never URL-checked; iframe allow is allowlisted; vbscript: passes.
findings.evidence: probe.mjs rows: 'meta refresh (no removals)' -> <meta http-equiv=refresh> in output; 'link stylesheet (no removals)' -> <link rel=stylesheet href=attacker>; v2 'link import/preload [noremove]' same. Cause: meta/link only in EXACT_SELECTORS (constants.ts:100-101), not in UNSAFE_ELEMENT_TAGS (dom.ts:83-86); with standardize on, rel/http-equiv/content are dropped by ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES so default mode is inert. srcset/data-src/poster javascript: survive under standardize:false (URL_ATTRIBUTES dom.ts:96 omits them; srcset/data-src are in ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES constants.ts:1089-1090,1109); browsers do not execute javascript: in these, and markdown.ts:153 checks the selected srcset candidate. `<table background=javascript:>` survives under standardize:false (legacy attribute, inert in modern browsers). `allow="camera *; microphone *; geolocation *"` on an attacker iframe survives in DEFAULT mode (constants.ts:1082). vbscript: passes isDangerousUrl (IE-only). Exploitability: redirect/CSS-injection/permission-delegation/tracking only; deterministic fixes: add meta/link/form/base to UNSAFE tags unconditionally; URL-check srcset/data-src/data-srcset/poster/background/ping; drop or constrain allow; block vbscript:.

findings.claim: CSS/style gaps (measured): SVG elements keep `style` in every mode; a page-derived Tailwind `text-[...]` token is written verbatim into a style attribute in DEFAULT mode; Markdown complex tables keep style/bgcolor when standardize is off or via createMarkdownContent.
findings.evidence: src/standardize.ts:475-481 (SVG elements: only class removed, all other attributes kept) -> `<rect style="fill:url(https://attacker.example/t)">` survives in default/nostd/noremove (6/6 rows). src/standardize.ts:929-931 pushes `font-size:${match[1]}` from TW_ARBITRARY_RE (constants.ts:1184 /^text-\[(.+)\]$/) and :950-953 writes it into style -> class `text-[12px;background:url(https://attacker.example/t)]` becomes style="font-size:12px;background:url(https://attacker.example/t)" in DEFAULT mode (2/2 rows). src/markdown.ts:875 allowedAttributes includes 'style' and 'bgcolor' -> `<td style="position:fixed;...;background:url(...)">` survives with {markdown:true, standardize:false} and with createMarkdownContent direct (2/3 rows). Impact: external fetch (IP/tracking) and UI overlay in renderers honoring inline style; no script. Fix: allowlist CSS properties (fill/stroke/opacity/font-*) and reject `url(`/`position`; validate text-[...] against /^[\d.]+(px|rem|em|%)$/.

findings.claim: Scheme coverage: entity-encoded, whitespace/control-obfuscated, mixed-case javascript:, data:image/svg+xml on <a>, <use href=data:>, file:, about:, obsidian:// and custom schemes are handled acceptably or are browser-mitigated; only vbscript: (dead) and the quote-prefix ordering bug are real misses.
findings.evidence: isDangerousUrl (dom.ts:74) removes all \s and \u0000-\u001F before matching, so `java\tscript:`, ` javascript:`, `javascript:` (DOM-decoded) are caught (measured clean). data:image/* is allowed on any href/src except iframe src (:77, :132): `<a href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg onload>">` survives but Chrome/Firefox block top-frame navigation to data: URLs (Firefox explicitly excludes image/svg+xml from its allowlist), and `<use href=data:image/svg+xml>` referenced documents are script-disabled (inference from browser behavior, not executed here). file:/about:/custom schemes pass by design (relative and mailto must pass); risk is click-phishing only. Deterministic tightening: allow data: only on img/source/track/video/audio/svg image, never on <a>/<use>/<feImage>.

findings.claim: Defuddle's own latency budget makes a per-page remote decision call a 1-3x slowdown of the whole pipeline, and the browser bundle is synchronous and offline by contract.
findings.evidence: Measured perf-baseline.json (226 fixtures, linkedom, Node 22, single run, no warm-up): p50 148.8 ms, p90 608 ms, p99 4337 ms, max 7979 ms (general--substack-app.html, 68 KB). Jev independent p50: 175 ms direct at 2.6k tokens (OpenRouter), 300-500 ms with a few k tokens or via gateway, 524 ms Cloudflare-measured median (JEV_ECOSYSTEM_EXCERPTS_1 s5). Browser API `new Defuddle(document).parse()` is synchronous (SCOUT_NOTES); CLI/fixture tests are hermetic; website/src/privacy.ts:31 promises 'The npm package and browser extension run entirely locally and make no network requests'; no browser-safe key mode exists for Jev (brief s3: a key shipped in client code is exposed).

findings.claim: Jev as the sanitization gate would subtract from security: the model evaluates argued input it cannot verify, cannot see what later code does to a value, is non-deterministic, and fails exactly on adversarially obfuscated strings.
findings.evidence: Brief s8 rule 1-3 and excerpts: state is untrusted argued input; routing accuracy 100% -> 0-5.8% under injection (ASR 93.5-100%, Wang et al.); one appended opinion flips 12.1% (JevAdvBench); 'Page text is untrusted data, never instructions' did not stop 91% planted-ad clicks (HiddenLayer); TokenBreak-respelled prompts passed its toxicity filter; attacked decisions were as confident as originals so confidence gating does not catch attacks; 12% chosen-option change on repeat, no seeds, version drift; 'Jev evaluates what is in the state; it does not simulate what is absent' (Yang et al.). Applied here: the confirmed bypass is `"javascript:` followed by a code-side quote strip; a Noul asked 'is this URL dangerous?' sees a quote-prefixed string that is in fact inert until resolve() runs, so a correct literal answer is 'no'. 32k-token per-question cap vs fixtures up to 201,904 bytes forces truncation, and a payload can be placed past the cut. Fail-closed on 429/529/outage would drop all content; fail-open adds nothing.

findings.claim: Jev as a secondary detector/telemetry is feasible only on the Worker, adds little beyond the exact deterministic oracle, and costs roughly 6-10% of per-request revenue plus 300-500 ms.
findings.evidence: Cloudflare Workers AI exposes `typesafe/jev` (jev-1.13.0, ZDR yes, $0.042/M in) so the Worker could ask Nouls like 'contains a login form', 'contains a redirect to another site', 'contains obfuscated markup' for logging. Cost: a 7k-token page ~ $0.0003 vs defuddle.md price $0.003-0.005/request (SCOUT_NOTES). The exact oracle (spec-parser round trip + scan for on*, forbidden elements, dangerous schemes), as implemented in roundtrip-v2.mjs, already detects 100% of the XSS-class constructs with zero false positives on the 33 payload variants the strict scorer demoted; Jev can only add semantic categories outside the XSS threat model (phishing, lookalike). No labeled corpus exists for shadow mode (SCOUT_NOTES: ground truth is 226 expected outputs, none labeled for security). Oct 24 2026 leak exposed all customers' Noul outputs, so even telemetry outputs are a disclosure surface.

findings.claim: Jev as a fuzz-test oracle is dominated by an exact oracle; the exact oracle found a real bypass in 433 probes with no model.
findings.evidence: A security test oracle must be exact and reproducible; Jev moves 0.04 probability on repeats and 12% of chosen options, reads obfuscated strings poorly (TokenBreak), cannot parse or count (brief s7), and the brief's own cookbook calls RAG screening 'a filter, not a security boundary'. roundtrip-v2.mjs (serialize -> JSDOM/parse5 re-parse -> attribute/element scan, both input parsers) is deterministic, ~70 s for 433 rows, and surfaced the strip-before-resolve bypass plus the Tailwind style injection. Marginal Jev use: clustering fuzzer-found diffs for human triage; existing corpora (DOMPurify tests, PortSwigger cheat sheet) are already categorized, so value is low.

findings.claim: Bundle headroom rules out a heavy drop-in library for the core browser bundle without raising budgets, but a purpose-built allowlist serializer fits.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs:7-10 budgets: dist/index.js 92 KB, dist/index.full.js 215 KB gzip; measured now: 89.8 KB and 207.1 KB (2.2 KB and 7.9 KB headroom). DOMPurify-class library is on the order of 8-10 KB gzip (inference, not measured here); an allowlist serializer over the existing ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES set plus a per-attribute URL policy is ~1-2 KB (inference).

caveats: No real browser or Obsidian/Electron execution was performed; the oracle is a static re-parse with JSDOM/parse5 plus attribute/element scanning. Statements like 'img src=javascript: is inert' and 'top-frame data: navigation is blocked' rest on known browser behavior, not on runs here.

The 'strict' oracle treats a value as dangerous only when its parsed scheme is javascript:/vbscript:/blob:/non-image data:; values with a literal leading quote (e.g. after createMarkdownContent, which never resolves URLs) were classified inert. If some downstream consumer strips quotes the way defuddle's resolve() does, those would become live too.

Whether the Obsidian Web Clipper renders defuddle's HTML `content` or converts it to Markdown itself could not be verified from this repository; Markdown consumers are shown to be protected, HTML consumers are not.

Perf baseline is a single unwarmed run on this machine with linkedom under Node 22 and includes any per-fixture retry cascades; browser timings will differ. It is used only for order-of-magnitude comparison with published Jev latencies.

Jev figures (latency, ASR, non-determinism, leak) are taken from the supplied brief and excerpts, not measured by me; no live Jev calls were made in this slice because the security argument does not depend on Jev's accuracy.

The 25-extractor exposure is by code path (all route through _sanitizeExtractorHtml); only x-article was exercised end to end. The _serializeFallbackBody path was exercised directly; triggering it through the public API requires an exception or null result in _parse(), which I did not demonstrate.
The earlier attempt's probe.mjs/probe2.mjs/probe-jsdom.mjs and their JSON were reused for 126 rows; I re-scored them and independently reproduced their key result in roundtrip-v2.mjs.
The repository was not modified (git status clean apart from untracked dist/); all artifacts are under /tmp/jev-research/results/security-map/.

result.verdict_for_this_dimension: Do not use Jev for security sanitization (meaning A), at any aggressiveness. Every historical defect (5 GHSAs) and the one confirmed today (strip-before-resolve on _sanitizeExtractorHtml and _serializeFallbackBody, exploitable through the schema.org fallback and all 25 site extractors, and an origin XSS on defuddle.md /html/) is a coverage or ordering omission in deterministic code; a probabilistic, non-deterministic, injectable, remote model cannot close that class and would add latency (1-3x the whole parse), privacy exposure, an offline/sync-API break, and a new path to miss. The route to ~99.99% is deterministic: fix the two ordering bugs immediately; funnel all five HTML boundaries through one typed finalizer that strips last; replace the denylist with an allowlist serializer with a per-attribute URL policy (data: only on media attributes; meta/link/base/form/style gone regardless of options; CSS property allowlist on SVG/table style); add the spec-parser round-trip differential test (linkedom + JSDOM + a real browser) and property-based fuzzing to CI; and put a CSP sandbox plus nosniff on defuddle.md /html/ responses so a sanitizer miss can no longer become origin XSS. The only tolerable Jev role is Worker-side telemetry that never influences output, and it earns little over the exact oracle.

result.title: Jev keep-vs-clutter block classification vs defuddle fixtures: V1 (HTML), V2 (text), V3 (JSON+context) on 1,475 units, two ground truths, confidence-band and page-level analysis
result.summary:
What I did. The live runs for this slice already existed in /tmp/jev-research/results/exp-block-classification/ (raw-v1.jsonl 1,475 units, raw-v2/v3 767 units each on the fixed-seed subsample, plus a 767-unit V1 repeat; all jev-1.14.0, 0 errors). Rather than re-spend, I verified them by re-querying 12 random units (12/12 same model, identical input-token counts, mean |dp| 0.005, 0 decision flips) and reused them. I then found that the dataset's ground truth was partly wrong: build-block-dataset.mjs derives 'kept/removed' by shingle-matching unit text against `outDoc.body.textContent` of defuddle's output (line 103), which glues adjacent block elements ("YouTube UI↩That's to say"), so short units (headings, footnote items, list items) lost their shingles and were labeled 'removed' although tests/expected/<fixture>.md keeps them verbatim. I wrote relabel.mjs (whitespace-correct match against both defuddle output and the expected Markdown body): 72 of 367 'removed' units flip to 'kept', 0 flip the other way, 20 become 'mixed' and are excluded. I re-ran a full analysis (analyze2.mjs) under both GT-A (original labels, as specified) and GT-B (corrected), with fixture-clustered bootstrap CIs, two threshold-tuning splits (by unit and by fixture), confidence bands split into content-loss vs clutter-leak errors, cascades at 0.8/0.9/0.94/0.98, and hand judgments for 77 disagreements (both top-40 lists plus every confident-band disagreement under GT-B).

What I found (measured). Jev is a competent but not heuristic-beating standalone classifier. V1 (block HTML) on all units: GT-A accuracy 0.837 at 0.5, AUROC 0.838, F1(removed) 0.645; GT-B accuracy 0.876 [95% CI 0.822-0.914], AUROC 0.891 [0.849-0.923], F1(removed) 0.688, F1(kept) 0.922, ECE 0.068; tuned thresholds (cross-fit, both splits land at p_keep≈0.25-0.32, i.e. Jev under-states keep) raise accuracy to 0.904-0.907. Excluding policy removals (title/byline/date, which defuddle handles deterministically) and site-extractor pages: accuracy 0.929, AUROC 0.948, tuned 0.952. Confidence is informative: |2p-1|≥0.8 covers 66.5% of units at 93.9% agreement (GT-B; 98.1% on the non-policy/non-extractor subset), ≥0.9 covers 42.6% at 96.1%, ≥0.94 covers 19.5% at 99.3%, ≥0.98 covers 0.3%. Text-only state (V2) is best calibrated (ECE 0.047) and most accurate in-band (95.9%) but least confident (38.7% coverage); adding page_title/url as JSON (V3) made Jev more confident and less accurate (AUROC 0.883→0.856 on the same units, 57 confident clutter leaks vs 32) — context stuffed into the state did not help. Repeats are stable (mean |dp| 0.008, 0.8% decision flips, 0 confident contradictions). Cost: 981 tokens/call, $0.061 for all 1,475 blocks, p50 latency 70 ms, p90 106 ms, p99 173 ms at concurrency 8.

Error analysis (judged). Under GT-B, 59 of the 967 confident-band units disagree with the fixtures; by hand: 21 are the page-title h1 (a defuddle policy Jev was never told about), 17 are comment/extractor pages (HN, Reddit, GitHub PR, Gmail) where the literal instruction "do not keep comment sections / dates" is wrong for the page type, 4 are index-listing card metadata, 8 are residual label artifacts (code blocks with line-number gutters, math converted to LaTeX), 1 is a confirmed defuddle bug (footnotes--wikipedia-references: the last body paragraph before "See also" is removed by removeThinPrecedingSection, src/removals/content-patterns.ts:197-215, and the human-reviewed expected file encodes the loss; Jev said keep at p=0.98), 4 are ambiguous (3 leaning Jev), and only 4 are genuine Jev errors (0.4% of the band; 3 would be content loss: an inline "Share this article" link judged out of context, a list item literally reading "Google docs comments", a GitHub PR description judged as a comment). The top-40 list under the original labels is dominated by label artifacts (20) and title policy (8); the previous analysis's headline accuracy (0.837) understated Jev by about 4 points for that reason.

What it implies for the Jev question. (1) Jev cannot replace defuddle's clutter removal: at any threshold it disagrees with the test-verified output on 9-12% of blocks, with page-level perfection on only 56-62% of fixtures, and the "99.99%" target is unreachable (99%+ agreement only below 20% coverage). (2) Layered as a confident-only second opinion (|2p-1|≥0.9 or ≥0.94) with code handling titles, bylines/dates and extractor/comment pages, Jev would contradict a correct pipeline on roughly 0.4-0.8% of the blocks it decides, and in the one case where the pipeline was demonstrably wrong it was confidently right; the inverse rate (how often Jev is confidently right when the heuristic is wrong) cannot be measured on this corpus because the corpus is the heuristic's own output. (3) Weak spots: 3-15-word units (accuracy 0.76-0.83 vs 0.95-0.98 for 16-100 words), site-extractor pages (gmail 0.31, github 0.50, hackernews 0.57), literal keyword triggers ("comments"), and instruction-driven policy mismatches; strengths: prose paragraphs (p tags 0.965, 3 errors in 475 confident decisions), nav/header/footer (100%), removeBySelector removals (recall 0.918). The practical value demonstrated is as a shadow-mode regression detector (flag confident-keep on removed blocks), not as an authority in the pipeline.

findings.claim: Repeat stability on 767 units (same state, questions, model): 49.2% identical probabilities, mean |dp| 0.008, p90 0.02, max 0.10, 0.8% decision flips at 0.5, 0.8% kind flips, 2.9% band-membership changes, 0 confident contradictions.

findings.claim: Inference: Jev would be most useful to defuddle as a shadow-mode regression detector (confident keep on a removed block = candidate over-stripping, confident remove on a kept long block = candidate leak), gated at |2p-1|>=0.9, with titles, bylines/dates, hidden elements and extractor/comment pages excluded by code; it should not be the primary decider, and nothing in this data supports a '~99.99% reliable' claim for clutter removal.
findings.evidence: Derived from the band/cascade/judgment numbers above; 99%+ agreement only at <20% coverage; genuine confident error rate 0.4-0.8%.

caveats: Ground truth is defuddle's own test-verified output, so the heuristic is 100% 'correct' by construction; this measures agreement, not which system is better. The one place the two can be compared independently (fixture errors) yielded a single instance.

Original labels (GT-A) contain a systematic builder bug (glued textContent); GT-B fixes 72 units but still has residual artifacts (code blocks with line-number gutters, KaTeX/LaTeX math) which I identified by hand only in the confident band (8 units); 20 'mixed' units were excluded from GT-B.

Fixtures are mostly small synthetic regression cases (median 1.7 KB, 6.5 units per fixture); a handful of real pages (lesswrong 213 units, maggieappleton 99, x.com 43, wikipedia 37) dominate some breakdowns. Results are not a web-scale estimate; fixture-clustered bootstrap CIs are wide (band accuracy 0.899-0.965).

Units were segmented by the dataset builder (largest homogeneous block <=300 words), not by where defuddle actually makes removal decisions; an integration would ask different questions about different nodes.
The V2/V3 subsample is class-enriched (37% removed vs 19% in the population), so its accuracies are not comparable to all-unit accuracy; AUROC and in-band precision are comparable.

Threshold tuning used one seed per split; the fixture split under GT-A produced unstable thresholds (0.255 vs 0.555), so tuned numbers should be read as indicative. Reported tuned metrics are cross-fit (each half scored with the other half's threshold).

Hand judgments (77 units) are one reviewer's reading of the fixtures; the remaining 110 (GT-A) / 70 (GT-B) low-confidence disagreements were auto-categorized (title/extractor/byline) or left unjudged.

Jev was given a single literal instruction; it was never told defuddle's policies (title to frontmatter, comment pages are content, index pages kept whole, hidden elements removed via CSS), so a large share of disagreements are instruction design, not model capability. A page-type-aware prompt was not tested; adding page_title/url to the state (V3) hurt rather than helped.
No adversarial/prompt-injection test was run in this slice; the state is page-derived HTML, which the brief says must be treated as untrusted.

Raw API results come from an earlier run in this same experiment folder (record timestamps 2026-10-27T22:33-22:37Z) and were reused after a 12-unit re-query confirmed consistency; latency figures are from this host at concurrency 8 and include no gateway hop.
Cost uses the published $0.042 per million input tokens; output tokens (about 144 per call) were counted but are free.

result.verdict_for_this_dimension: Measured: Jev (jev-1.14.0, one literal Noul + one 12-way Choice per block, ~1k tokens, 70 ms, $0.00004 per block) agrees with defuddle's test-verified keep/remove decisions on 87.6% of 1,455 blocks at p=0.5 (AUROC 0.891) once the dataset's own labeling bug is corrected, 92.9% (AUROC 0.948) when page titles/bylines/dates and site-extractor pages are left to code. That is not 'at least as well as the heuristics' in the sense of replacing them (the heuristic is 100% by construction and Jev disagrees on 7-12% of blocks, perfect on only 56-62% of pages), and nothing approaches 99.99%: 99%+ agreement exists only at |2p-1|>=0.94, which covers 19.5% of blocks. Where Jev is confident (|2p-1|>=0.8, 66% of blocks) it agrees 93.9% (98.1% on non-policy, non-extractor pages), and hand review of every confident disagreement shows the residual is overwhelmingly policy Jev was never told (page title to frontmatter 21, comment/mail/PR pages 17, index-page card metadata 4), dataset artifacts (8), or a genuine defuddle bug Jev caught (1); only 4 of 967 confident decisions (0.4%) are real Jev errors, 3 of which would delete content. Inference: Jev should not be wired in as the clutter decider (short 3-15-word units, extractor pages and literal keyword triggers like 'comments' are its failure modes, and context in the state made it over-confident rather than better), but a confident-only, shadow-mode second opinion gated at >=0.9/0.94 with titles, hidden elements and page type handled in code is cheap, stable across repeats (0.8% flips), and demonstrably able to flag over-stripping regressions the fixtures themselves missed. 'Aggressive' use is not supported by this data.

result.title: Cost / latency / limits model for four Jev integration shapes (measured on 226 Defuddle fixtures, dist build, linkedom; no API calls)
result.summary:
I measured every one of the 226 fixtures in /home/alexi/git/defuddle/tests/fixtures with the compiled Node build (dist/node.js -> dist/defuddle.js, linkedom 0.18.12, Node 22.20): raw bytes, cleaned-HTML bytes (script/style/noscript/template, comments, SVG path data, base64 data: URIs and >200-char attribute values stripped, whitespace collapsed), body text bytes, token estimates (HTML bytes/3.5, text bytes/4 — stated assumptions), labeled units from /tmp/jev-research/results/dataset/blocks.jsonl, ENTRY_POINT_ELEMENTS candidates counted exactly as findMainContent does (src/defuddle.ts:1247-1256), and which _parseWithRetries branches fire (captured from the debug console.log lines at src/defuddle.ts:103/122/140/164/197/203). I also ran the repo perf test once (unmodified; vitest hid console output on the first run, so it was re-run with --silent=false). Scripts and raw outputs are under /tmp/jev-research/results/measure-cost/.

The fixture set is dominated by tiny synthetic cases: median raw 1,755 B, median cleaned-body ~412 HTML tokens, median 3 labeled units. Only 14 fixtures exceed 20 KB raw ("real" group: median 53.6 KB raw, 12.6k HTML tokens, 1.5k text tokens, 28 units, parse 92 ms). The ten largest are mathjax (202 KB), lesswrong (150 KB), maggieappleton (130 KB), x.com article (123 KB), github issue (105 KB), 12gramsofcarbon (98 KB), substack-app (68 KB), katex-centraliser (54 KB), figma blog (45 KB), obsidian blog (32 KB). Because the synthetic fixtures are short, the first retry branch (wordCount < 200, src/defuddle.ts:102) fires on 178/226 (78.8%) fixtures but is accepted on only 3; across all branches a retry is accepted on 11/226 (4.9%). On the real group any retry fires on 1/14 and the final pick is plain `html > body` on 3/14. A "retry fired or body pick" gate therefore fires on 82% of fixtures (loose) or 32-36% (strict: <50-word branches, schema, body pick, excluding extractor pages whose empty selector is by design) — it is not a selective trigger.

Shape costs at $0.042/M: S2 (one container Choice, ~2k tokens) is $0.000084/page = $0.084 per 1,000 pages and adds ~250 ms. S1c (one request per page, N Nouls over an id-annotated cleaned page) costs $0.53/1,000 on the real-fixture median and an extrapolated $0.75-2.00/1,000 for 15k-40k-token real pages, adds ~500 ms, but 2/14 real fixtures (14%) and, by extrapolation, roughly half of 50-500 KB real-world pages exceed the 32k per-question limit (breakpoint ~164 KB raw at the real group's median cleaned/raw ratio 0.68), forcing chunking. S1 (one request per block) costs about the same tokens as S1c ($0.55/1,000 real median, $0.91-2.41/1,000 extrapolated) but is request-rate bound: 28-114 requests per page means 7-28 s sequential or 1-3.75 s at 8-concurrent per page, and only 0.28-0.71 pages/s (1,000-2,600 pages/hour) under the community-cited 1,200 req/min limit. S3 gated (strict gate, 32-36%) brings expected cost to ~$0.03/1,000 under S2 or ~$0.26/1,000 under S1c on real pages. S4 (S1+S2 everywhere) is $0.63/1,000 (real median) to $1.6-2.5/1,000 extrapolated.

Against defuddle.md's $0.003-0.005 per request: S2 is 1.7-2.8% of revenue; S1/S1c on a typical 25k-token page are 25-50%; on a 40k-token page S1/S4 reach 48-83%. Against current parse time (dist: median 21 ms all fixtures, 92 ms real group; vitest: 16 ms median, 355 ms max; total 6.4 s across 226 fixtures, removeBySelector 23% and findMainContent 10% of step time), every shape adds at least 250 ms, i.e. 2.7x the real-group median parse, and S1 adds 11x+ at 8-concurrent. Implication for the Jev question: dollar cost is immaterial for a single container-level Choice or a gated check, significant but not prohibitive for per-block judgments on a paid service, and the real constraints are latency (any shape multiplies parse time), the 32k per-question window (half of real pages need chunking for HTML-state block judgments), the request-rate ceiling (per-block requests cap throughput at ~1,000 pages/hour), and the fact that Defuddle's existing retry signals are far too noisy to serve as a confidence gate without redesign.

findings.claim: The fixture corpus is overwhelmingly small synthetic pages; only 14/226 exceed 20 KB raw, so per-page cost figures from the full set understate real-world cost by roughly 10-20x.
